accounts\[KEY\].  
**t\_side**  
  
enum

 | 

The side of the balance sheet where the Account balance is counted. Can be optionally provided when creating Internal Accounts. If it is not provided, it will default to LIABILITY. For Customer Accounts, the t\_side is defined in the Smart Contract. It cannot be provided in this request.  
  
**Enum values**  
**T\_SIDE\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default Value, invalid.  
**T\_SIDE\_ASSET:**  
Debit postings increase balances for asset Accounts.  
**T\_SIDE\_LIABILITY:**  
Credit postings increase balances for liability Accounts.

The most recent time at which the Smart Contract Version was updated on the Account, in UTC. Empty if it has never changed. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. The value corresponds to the `effective_datetime` hook argument when the conversion hook was last run.

## [](#adjustments "Copy link to heading")Adjustments

Adjustments retroactively correct an Account’s balances in response to backdated events.

For more information, see the [Adjustments](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/adjustments) section.

### [](#adjustment "Copy link to heading")Adjustment

#### [](#available_methods_11 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_ListAdjustmentsResponse_ListAdjustments) Pages through an ordered list of Adjustments based on filtering criteria.
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_BatchGetAdjustmentsResponse_BatchGetAdjustments) Retrieves a set of Adjustments by their IDs.
    
-   [BulkRetry](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_BulkRetryAdjustmentsResponse_BulkRetryAdjustments) This API can be used to retry Adjustments with status of ERROR.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_ListAdjustmentsResponse_ListAdjustments "Copy link to heading")List

Pages through an ordered list of Adjustments based on filtering criteria. The request must filter by either Account or Schedule Job ID.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.adjustments:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Page Level

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/adjustments

##### [](#request_29 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of results to be listed per page. Required; must have an integer value in the range 1-100.

 |
| 

**page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

Token of the page to retrieve. If empty, returns the first page of results. This should only be populated using values from a previous response’s previous or next page token.

 |
| 

**account\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

This will filter the results to all Adjustments for a particular set of Customer Accounts. It cannot be combined with Schedule Job IDs filter, and is required if there are no Schedule Job IDs provided.

 |
| 

**schedule\_job\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

This will filter results to all adjustments on the Schedule Job ID which triggered them. It cannot be combined with the account IDs filter, and is required if no Account IDs are provided.

 |

Success Errors

adjustments\[\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status reflects the Adjustment’s progress, and whether it has failed due to an error, been discarded as unnecessary, or completed successfully.  
  
**Enum values**  
**STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
This is a default value and will not appear in any responses.  
**STATUS\_PENDING:**  
The Account has had backdates that could mean a correction is required.  
**STATUS\_RUNNING:**  
The history of the Account is being simulated to determine whether any corrections are necessary.  
**STATUS\_COMPLETED:**  
The Account has been corrected (if necessary) and its Schedule Job is now unblocked; terminal state.  
**STATUS\_NO\_ADJUSTMENT\_REQUIRED:**  
The Account has not had any backdates that could mean a correction is required; terminal state.  
**STATUS\_ERROR:**  
The Adjustment has encountered an error. The POST /v1/adjustments:bulkRetry endpoint can be used to retry an Adjustment with this status. The Schedule Job will not execute until the Adjustment terminates.

 |

adjustments\[\].  
error.  
**code**  
  
enum

 | 

The code of the error.  
  
**Enum values**  
**OK:**  
Indicates there was no error. In practice, this does not occur as success is communicated by the absence of an error rather than an error with this code.  
**CANCELLED:**  
The requested operation was cancelled part way through.  
**UNKNOWN:**  
An unknown problem occurred on the server.  
**INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
There was a problem with the request. A provided field is invalid and/or a required field is missing. Unlike FAILED\_PRECONDITION, the only remedy is likely to be a change to the request.  
**DEADLINE\_EXCEEDED:**  
The response was not received within the allowed time. It can be safely retried. The operation could have completed successfully.  
**NOT\_FOUND:**  
The requested resource could not be found.  
**ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
The resource could not be created because it already exists.  
**PERMISSION\_DENIED:**  
The client did not have permission to perform the request.  
**UNAUTHENTICATED:**  
The request could not be authenticated.  
**RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED:**  
A resource was exhausted, because either too many requests were sent within a time period or the response was too large.  
**FAILED\_PRECONDITION:**  
The operation was rejected because the system was not in a state required for the operation’s execution. It could be that a referenced resource did not exist, or was in the wrong state.  
**ABORTED:**  
The operation was aborted, typically due to a concurrency issue.  
**OUT\_OF\_RANGE:**  
The operation was attempted outside the valid range.  
**UNIMPLEMENTED:**  
The operation is not implemented.  
**INTERNAL:**  
A problem occurred on the server. This is almost certainly due to a fault in the platform.  
**UNAVAILABLE:**  
The service was unavailable. It can be safely retried.  
**DATA\_LOSS:**  
The operation resulted in unrecoverable data loss or corruption.

details\[\].  
**type\_url**  
  
string

 | 

A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least one "/" character. The last segment of the URL’s path must represent the fully qualified name of the type (as in `path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form (e.g., leading "." is not accepted).  
  
In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:  
  
\* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed. \* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a \[google.protobuf.Type\]\[\] value in binary format, or produce an error. \* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage breaking changes.)  
  
Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with type.googleapis.com.  
  
Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be used with implementation specific semantics.

An Adjustment operates on a period of time dictated by the value/effective time of a backdate, though limited by when the Account was created on, or converted to, an Adjustments-enabled Smart Contract. If an Account has multiple conversions in its history from a Smart Contract not enabled for Adjustments to one that is, the most recent such conversion is used for the lower bound.

#### [](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_BatchGetAdjustmentsResponse_BatchGetAdjustments "Copy link to heading")BatchGet

Retrieves a set of Adjustments by their IDs.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.adjustments:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/adjustments:batchGet

##### [](#request_30 "Copy link to heading")Request

The retrieved Adjustments. This is a map of Adjustments keyed on ID.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

This is a UUID that uniquely identifies this Adjustment. It is randomly generated by Vault Core and any value provided in a creation request will be ignored.

 |

adjustments\[KEY\].

string

 | 

The ID of the Schedule Job which created this Adjustment.

The number of Adjustments created so far for the Account, regardless of the status of each Adjustment.

string

 | 

The ID of the account that is the target of the Adjustment.

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status reflects the Adjustment’s progress, and whether it has failed due to an error, been discarded as unnecessary, or completed successfully.  
  
**Enum values**  
**STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
This is a default value and will not appear in any responses.  
**STATUS\_PENDING:**  
The Account has had backdates that could mean a correction is required.  
**STATUS\_RUNNING:**  
The history of the Account is being simulated to determine whether any corrections are necessary.  
**STATUS\_COMPLETED:**  
The Account has been corrected (if necessary) and its Schedule Job is now unblocked; terminal state.  
**STATUS\_NO\_ADJUSTMENT\_REQUIRED:**  
The Account has not had any backdates that could mean a correction is required; terminal state.  
**STATUS\_ERROR:**  
The Adjustment has encountered an error. The POST /v1/adjustments:bulkRetry endpoint can be used to retry an Adjustment with this status. The Schedule Job will not execute until the Adjustment terminates.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**error**  
  
object

 | 

If the Adjustment is in status ERROR, then this will be populated with the error that caused it.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
error.  
**message**  
  
string

 | 

A human-readable description of the error. The exact message is subject to change and should not be used programmatically.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
error.  
**code**  
  
enum

 | 

The code of the error.  
  
**Enum values**  
**OK:**  
Indicates there was no error. In practice, this does not occur as success is communicated by the absence of an error rather than an error with this code.  
**CANCELLED:**  
The requested operation was cancelled part way through.  
**UNKNOWN:**  
An unknown problem occurred on the server.  
**INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
There was a problem with the request. A provided field is invalid and/or a required field is missing. Unlike FAILED\_PRECONDITION, the only remedy is likely to be a change to the request.  
**DEADLINE\_EXCEEDED:**  
The response was not received within the allowed time. It can be safely retried. The operation could have completed successfully.  
**NOT\_FOUND:**  
The requested resource could not be found.  
**ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
The resource could not be created because it already exists.  
**PERMISSION\_DENIED:**  
The client did not have permission to perform the request.  
**UNAUTHENTICATED:**  
The request could not be authenticated.  
**RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED:**  
A resource was exhausted, because either too many requests were sent within a time period or the response was too large.  
**FAILED\_PRECONDITION:**  
The operation was rejected because the system was not in a state required for the operation’s execution. It could be that a referenced resource did not exist, or was in the wrong state.  
**ABORTED:**  
The operation was aborted, typically due to a concurrency issue.  
**OUT\_OF\_RANGE:**  
The operation was attempted outside the valid range.  
**UNIMPLEMENTED:**  
The operation is not implemented.  
**INTERNAL:**  
A problem occurred on the server. This is almost certainly due to a fault in the platform.  
**UNAVAILABLE:**  
The service was unavailable. It can be safely retried.  
**DATA\_LOSS:**  
The operation resulted in unrecoverable data loss or corruption.

**type\_url**  
  
string

 | 

A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least one "/" character. The last segment of the URL’s path must represent the fully qualified name of the type (as in `path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form (e.g., leading "." is not accepted).  
  
In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:  
  
\* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed. \* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a \[google.protobuf.Type\]\[\] value in binary format, or produce an error. \* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage breaking changes.)  
  
Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with type.googleapis.com.  
  
Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be used with implementation specific semantics.

error.

byte

adjustments\[KEY\].

dateTime

The time at which this Adjustment was created.

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**update\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The timestamp of the most recent status update of this Adjustment.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**previous\_watermark\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

An Adjustment checks for backdates that were inserted into Vault Core within a certain time range. This is the inclusive lower bound of that time range. For an Account’s first Adjustment it will be empty.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**timeline\_start\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

An Adjustment operates on a period of time dictated by the value/effective time of a backdate, though limited by when the Account was created on, or converted to, an Adjustments-enabled Smart Contract. This is the lower bound of that time period, and will be equal to either the earliest value/effective time, or the activation/conversion time of the Account. If an Account has multiple conversions in its history from a Smart Contract not enabled for Adjustments to one that is, the most recent such conversion is used for the lower bound.  
  
Returns null if Vault Core evaluates that an Adjustment is not required.

 |
| 

adjustments\[KEY\].  
**timeline\_end\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

The upper bound of the period of time simulated by the Adjustment.

#### [](#_core_api_v1_adjustments_BulkRetryAdjustmentsResponse_BulkRetryAdjustments "Copy link to heading")BulkRetry

This API can be used to retry Adjustments with status of ERROR. A retried Adjustment will first move to status PENDING before then proceeding through the normal processing stages. To identify errored Adjustments, consume from the Core Streaming API topic vault.core\_api.v1.adjustments.adjustment.events.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.adjustments:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/adjustments:bulkRetry

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:  
  
\* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed. \* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a \[google.protobuf.Type\]\[\] value in binary format, or produce an error. \* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage breaking changes.)  
  
Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with type.googleapis.com.  
  
Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be used with implementation specific semantics.

## [](#auth "Copy link to heading")Auth

**Deprecated:** Service Accounts and Service Account Authentication Tokens were deprecated as of release 4.3, and will be removed no earlier than release 7.0. *This deprecation is in favour of using JWT Tokens.*

Auth endpoints let other systems integrate with Vault using service accounts. Each service account has a list of permissions that indicate which endpoints it can access. The permission names map to the public gRPC names of an operation instead of the HTTP one; for example /core\_api.v1.accounts.CoreAPIAccounts/GetAccount. The gRPC endpoint takes into consideration, implicitly, the HTTP method (such as GET or PUT) of the endpoint.

This means it is often easier to configure service account permissions in the Operations Dashboard. If managed through the API instead of the Operations Dashboard, you must ensure an up-to-date list of available permissions is retrieved after a release.

When a new instance of Vault is created, a default service account is used to bootstrap the system and set up the initial service accounts. This operation should be performed by a trusted operator.

error

We do not recommend disabling the default service account without speaking with your Client Delivery Manager.

To create a service account, make a POST request to /v1/service-accounts including the name and its permissions. The endpoint will return a token that can subsequently be used to call the rest of the API.

For security reasons, Vault cannot reproduce this token. This means the token won’t be available when listing the service accounts.

If required, the status of the service account can then be updated to FROZEN or INACTIVE using a PUT to /v1/service-accounts/\\{service\_account.id}. Permissions can be added or removed using /v1/service-accounts/{service\_account\_id}:updatePermissions.

### [](#serviceaccount "Copy link to heading")ServiceAccount

#### [](#available_methods_12 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_auth_ListServiceAccountsResponse_ListServiceAccounts) Lists service accounts with pagination. **(Deprecated)**
    
-   [Create](#_core_api_v1_auth_ServiceAccount_CreateServiceAccount) Creates and returns a service account with the access token populated. **(Deprecated)**
    
-   [Get](#_core_api_v1_auth_ServiceAccount_GetServiceAccount) Retrieves the service account for the service account ID provided. **(Deprecated)**
    
-   [Update](#_core_api_v1_auth_ServiceAccount_UpdateServiceAccount) Updates a service account. **(Deprecated)**
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_auth_BatchGetServiceAccountsResponse_BatchGetServiceAccounts) Retrieves service accounts for the service account IDs provided. **(Deprecated)**
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_auth_ListServiceAccountsResponse_ListServiceAccounts "Copy link to heading")List

**Deprecated** as of release **4.3**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0** *This method is deprecated as Service Accounts have been deprecated in favour of JWT-based authentication*

#### [](#_core_api_v1_auth_ServiceAccount_UpdateServiceAccount "Copy link to heading")Update

**Deprecated** as of release **4.3**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0** *This method is deprecated as Service Accounts have been deprecated in favour of JWT-based authentication*

Updates a service account. The service account token will only be returned when the token is refreshed or if an inactive service account is reactivated. If an inactive service account is reactivated, a new token is generated. A service account with active status can be updated to be frozen or inactive. A service account with frozen status can be updated to active or inactive. If a frozen account is reactivated, a new token is not required. A service account with inactive status can only be updated to active status. Freezing a service account will disable existing tokens until the service account is reactivated. Deactivating a service account will permanently invalidate all previous tokens and new tokens will be required.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.service\_accounts:write

**Endpoint:** PUT /v1/service-accounts/{service\_account.id}

### [](#balancestimerange "Copy link to heading")BalancesTimeRange

#### [](#available_methods_16 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_balances_ListBalancesTimeRangeResponse_ListBalancesTimeRange) Retrieves a time range of balances for the supplied Customer Account IDs ordered by decreasing `value_time`.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_balances_ListBalancesTimeRangeResponse_ListBalancesTimeRange "Copy link to heading")List

Retrieves a time range of balances for the supplied Customer Account IDs ordered by decreasing `value_time`. If multiple entries have the same `value_time`, they will be grouped by balance definition, and within the groups the entries are ordered by decreasing logical time. This includes all balance events within the time range and the latest state of the balances as of the `from_time`, if provided, which could be prior to the time range.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.balances:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Snapshot

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/balances/timerange

| --- | --- |

array \[string\]

 |

 |
| 

**account\_addresses**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

Filters results by account address.

 |
| 

**from\_time**  
  
string

 | 

The earliest time in the time range of the returned balances in UTC. Optional. If included, will also return the latest balance event before the `from_time` for comparison. If omitted, the results will start from the first available balance event. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

**to\_time**  
  
string

 | 

The latest time in the time range of the returned balances in UTC. Optional. If omitted, the results will end at the last available balance event. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of results to be retrieved. Required.  
  
Required.

string

 |

 |
| 

**snapshot\_timestamp**  
  
string

 | 

If supplied, the balances time range will take into account only those postings inserted into Vault up to this time, and exclude balance changes from any postings inserted after this time. Optional.

 |

#### [](#_core_api_v1_calendar_BookkeepingDate_UpdateBookkeepingDate "Copy link to heading")Update

UpdateBookkeepingDate updates a Bookkeeping Date by the provided Calendar ID. This specifies what the next calendar period to be published should be annotated with.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.bookkeeping\_dates:write

**Endpoint:** PUT /v1/calendar/bookkeeping-date/{id}

### [](#calendarevent "Copy link to heading")CalendarEvent

#### [](#available_methods_22 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_calendar_ListCalendarEventsResponse_ListCalendarEvents) ListCalendarEvents retrieves a list of Calendar Events that occur within a specified time range.
    
-   [Create](#_core_api_v1_calendar_CalendarEvent_CreateCalendarEvent) CreateCalendarEvent creates a Calendar Event.
    
-   [Update](#_core_api_v1_calendar_CalendarEvent_UpdateCalendarEvent) UpdateCalendarEvent updates a Calendar Event based on a provided Calendar Event ID.
    
-   [Get](#_core_api_v1_calendar_CalendarEvent_GetCalendarEvent) GetCalendarEvent retrieves a Calendar Event using its ID.
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_calendar_BatchGetCalendarEventsResponse_BatchGetCalendarEvents) BatchGetCalendarEvents retrieves a list of Calendar Events using their IDs.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_calendar_ListCalendarEventsResponse_ListCalendarEvents "Copy link to heading")List

ListCalendarEvents retrieves a list of Calendar Events that occur within a specified time range.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.calendar\_events:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Best Effort

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/calendar-event

 |

 |

 |

integer

Required.

### [](#calendarperiod "Copy link to heading")CalendarPeriod

#### [](#available_methods_23 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [Calculate](#_core_api_v1_calendar_CalendarPeriod_CalculateCalendarPeriod) CalculateCalendarPeriod calculates the number of period resolution units from the start epoch of the Calendar to the given time and returns the expected Calendar Period data.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_calendar_CalendarPeriod_CalculateCalendarPeriod "Copy link to heading")Calculate

CalculateCalendarPeriod calculates the number of period resolution units from the start epoch of the Calendar to the given time and returns the expected Calendar Period data. Already-emitted Calendar Periods will be returned as-is.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.calendar\_periods:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/calendar/{calendar\_id}:calculatePeriod

##### [](#request_55 "Copy link to heading")Request

Path parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**calendar\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The Calendar ID that will be used when calculating the number of period resolution units from the Calendar’s start epoch.

 |

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**timestamp**  
  
string

 | 

The latest time that the number of period resolution units is calculated up to. Defaults to the current time in UTC. Must be formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |

##### [](#responses_20 "Copy link to heading")Responses

Success Errors

Response fields  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**expected\_end\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

End of the period, in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

**actual\_end\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

This timestamp will be updated when holding (pausing of given calendar) or rolling (advancing the period forward), for operational/accounting purposes. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp in UTC.

 |
| 

**period**  
  
long

 | 

A monotonically increasing value derived from the date and start\_period\_epoch timestamp.  
  
Required.

 |
| 

**expected\_start\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Start of current period, unmodified by hold/roll changes. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp in UTC.

 |
| 

**actual\_start\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Start of current period, affected by hold/roll of previous period. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp in UTC.

 |
| 

**calendar\_id**  
  
string

 | 

References the Calendar that the period belongs to.

 |
| 

**calendar\_period\_descriptor\_id**  
  
string

 | 

References the Calendar Period Descriptor that was used to generate the period.

 |
| 

**bookkeeping\_label**  
  
string

 | 

Bookkeeping label, in the ISO-8601 extended date format YYYY-MM-DD. This field is populated using the date from the most recently associated UpdateBookkeepingDate call.

 |

CreateCalendarPeriodDescriptor creates a Calendar Period Descriptor.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.calendar\_period\_descriptors:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/calendar-period-descriptor

##### [](#request_56 "Copy link to heading")Request

Body parameters

object

Required.

string

string

 |

object

 |

enum

## [](#contract_events "Copy link to heading")Contract Events

Contract Events are logical business journeys in Vault Core that require Smart or Supervisor Contract hook executions. A ContractExecution is an observation of a Smart or Supervisor Contract hook execution that occurred for a Contract Event.

warning

This endpoint provides observability data which is not guaranteed to be created after a Smart or Supervisor Contract hook execution. The data returned from this endpoint must not be relied upon by downstream integrations for financial processing.

For more information, see [Contract Events and the Contract Executions API](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/running_contracts_in_production).

### [](#contractexecution "Copy link to heading")ContractExecution

#### [](#available_methods_26 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_contract_events_ListContractExecutionsResponse_ListContractExecutions) Retrieves a filtered and paginated list of ContractExecution resources.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_contract_events_ListContractExecutionsResponse_ListContractExecutions "Copy link to heading")List

Retrieves a filtered and paginated list of ContractExecution resources.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.contract\_events:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Page Level

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/contract-executions

##### [](#request_58 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of ContractExecutions to be returned. Maximum 50. Required.  
  
Required.  
Min value: 1.  
Max value: 50.

 |
| 

**page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The token of the requested page, which comes from a previous GET v1/contract-events response. If empty, the first page will be returned. Optional.

 |
| 

**contract\_event\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

A set of Contract Event IDs. This filters ContractExecutions returned in the response to only those with a `contract_event_id` in the set. Must not contain IDs that are empty strings. Required if both `account_ids` and `plan_ids` are empty.  
  
Filters response to include only ContractExecutions that have field `contract_event_id` matching matching ANY `contract_event_id` provided in this set. Must not contain IDs that are empty strings. Required if both `account_ids` and `plan_ids` are empty.

 |
| 

**account\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

Filters response to include only ContractExecutions that have field `account_id` matching matching ANY `account_id` provided in this set. Must not contain IDs that are empty strings. Required if both `contract_event_ids` and `plan_ids` are empty.  
  
Note, specifying both `account_ids` and `plan_ids` filters will never return any Contract Executions, as a ContractExecution is associated with a single account or plan only. To list ContractExecutions that match any `account_ids` OR `plan_ids`, use the `or_fields` field and provide values `OR_FIELD_ACCOUNT_IDS` and `OR_FIELD_PLAN_IDS`.

 |
| 

**plan\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

Filters response to include only ContractExecutions that have field `plan_id` matching matching ANY `plan_id` provided in this set. Must not contain IDs that are empty strings. Required if both `contract_event_ids` and `account_ids` are empty.  
  
Note, specifying both `account_ids` and `plan_ids` filters will never return any Contract Executions, as a ContractExecution is associated with a single account or plan only. To list ContractExecutions that match any `account_ids` OR `plan_ids`, use the `or_fields` field and provide values `OR_FIELD_ACCOUNT_IDS` and `OR_FIELD_PLAN_IDS`.

 |
| 

**execution\_timestamp\_range**  
  
object

 | 

Optional. The timestamp range that the ContractExecution’s `execution_timestamp` must be within. This range is from `execution_timestamp_range.from` inclusive up to `execution_timestamp_range.to` exclusive. If `execution_timestamp_range.from` is not provided, defaults to the zero timestamp. If `execution_timestamp_range.to` is not provided, defaults to +inf.

 |
| 

execution\_timestamp\_range.  
**from**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Lower end of the range. The range is inclusive of its lower end.

 |
| 

execution\_timestamp\_range.  
**to**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Upper end of the range. The range is exclusive of its upper end.

 |
| 

**or\_fields**  
  
array \[enum\]

 | 

Optional. This field specifies that a ContractExecution should be returned if ANY of the following field filters match. This is opposed to the default behaviour, which only returns a ContractExecution is ALL field filters in the request are matched.  
  
**Enum values**  
**OR\_FIELD\_ACCOUNT\_IDS**  
**OR\_FIELD\_PLAN\_IDS**

 |

contract\_executions\[\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the execution.  
  
**Enum values**  
**STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
The status of the ContractExecution is unknown. This is invalid.  
**STATUS\_SUCCESS:**  
The ContractExecution succeeded, including the processing of any hook results.  
**STATUS\_SUCCESS\_NO\_HOOK:**  
The contract defined no hook for the contract event.  
**STATUS\_RETRYABLE\_EXECUTION\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution encountered a transient error when attempting to execute contract code.  
**STATUS\_EXECUTION\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution encountered a non-retryable execution error, such as contract syntax error.  
**STATUS\_HOOK\_RESULT\_RETURNED\_TO\_PARENT:**  
The ContractExecution successfully produced hook results, which were returned to the parent contract hook execution, i.e. a supervisor contract hook execution. The hook results of this ContractExecution have no effects on Vault, only parent ContractExecution hook results are committed to Vault.  
**STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The contract code returned a Rejection result, indicating that the Contract Event should not proceed. This is not a failure (error).  
**STATUS\_RETRYABLE\_HOOK\_RESULT\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution has successfully produced hook results, but none are committed to Vault due to encountering a transient error. This Contract Event will be retried automatically by Vault.  
**STATUS\_HOOK\_RESULT\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution has successfully produced hook results, but none are committed to Vault due to encountering a non-retryable error.  
**STATUS\_RETRYABLE\_HOOK\_RESULT\_PARTIAL\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution successfully produced hook results, then some hook results were successfully committed to Vault and have taken effect, but others have failed with a transient error. The Contract Event will be retried automatically by Vault.  
**STATUS\_HOOK\_RESULT\_PARTIAL\_ERROR:**  
The ContractExecution successfully produced hook results, then some hook results were successfully committed to Vault and have taken effect, but others have failed with a non-retryable error.

 |

**Enum values**  
**OK:**  
Indicates there was no error. In practice, this does not occur as success is communicated by the absence of an error rather than an error with this code.  
**CANCELLED:**  
The requested operation was cancelled part way through.  
**UNKNOWN:**  
An unknown problem occurred on the server.  
**INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
There was a problem with the request. A provided field is invalid and/or a required field is missing. Unlike FAILED\_PRECONDITION, the only remedy is likely to be a change to the request.  
**DEADLINE\_EXCEEDED:**  
The response was not received within the allowed time. It can be safely retried. The operation could have completed successfully.  
**NOT\_FOUND:**  
The requested resource could not be found.  
**ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
The resource could not be created because it already exists.  
**PERMISSION\_DENIED:**  
The client did not have permission to perform the request.  
**UNAUTHENTICATED:**  
The request could not be authenticated.  
**RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED:**  
A resource was exhausted, because either too many requests were sent within a time period or the response was too large.  
**FAILED\_PRECONDITION:**  
The operation was rejected because the system was not in a state required for the operation’s execution. It could be that a referenced resource did not exist, or was in the wrong state.  
**ABORTED:**  
The operation was aborted, typically due to a concurrency issue.  
**OUT\_OF\_RANGE:**  
The operation was attempted outside the valid range.  
**UNIMPLEMENTED:**  
The operation is not implemented.  
**INTERNAL:**  
A problem occurred on the server. This is almost certainly due to a fault in the platform.  
**UNAVAILABLE:**  
The service was unavailable. It can be safely retried.  
**DATA\_LOSS:**  
The operation resulted in unrecoverable data loss or corruption.

**type\_url**  
  
string

 | 

A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least one "/" character. The last segment of the URL’s path must represent the fully qualified name of the type (as in `path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form (e.g., leading "." is not accepted).  
  
In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:  
  
\* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed. \* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a \[google.protobuf.Type\]\[\] value in binary format, or produce an error. \* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage breaking changes.)  
  
Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with type.googleapis.com.  
  
Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be used with implementation specific semantics.

## [](#contract_modules "Copy link to heading")Contract Modules

Contract Modules are shared code modules that can be used by Smart Contracts to share common logic.

#### [](#available_methods_27 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_contract_modules_ListContractModulesResponse_ListContractModules) Lists Contract Modules.

## [](#contracts "Copy link to heading")Contracts

The Contracts endpoints allow you to simulate a given Smart Contract, producing a streaming output for a hypothetical account lifecycle. The simulation inputs are a) Smart Contract code (or a reference to it) and b) a series of time-stamped (past and future-dated) events, such as posting instruction batches, which target the account of interest. The instructions of (b) are called external or exogenous instructions and capture various hypothetical events that affect past and future financial behaviour of the account.

### [](#contract "Copy link to heading")Contract

#### [](#available_methods_30 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [Simulate](#_core_api_v1_contracts_SimulateContractsResponse_SimulateContracts) Simulates Smart Contracts
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_contracts_SimulateContractsResponse_SimulateContracts "Copy link to heading")Simulate

Simulates Smart Contracts

The response for this endpoint is streamed as new line separated JSON.

**Permission Scopes:** core:execute, core.contracts:execute

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/contracts:simulate

ExistingProductDataBehaviour is an optional field to control behaviour for whether or not simulation will fetch and include product data in simulation. Product data are data types available in contracts that are associated with products. That is, global parameters, template parameters, and calendar events.  
  
If unspecified, the default behaviour is to fetch and include no product data.  
  
If set, Simulation includes product data required by products specified in the request via: new or existing smart contracts, new or existing supervisor contracts, or existing smart contracts fetched due to specified existing accounts.

Note that if the simulated Smart Contracts specify that they require a particular data type, and it is neither specified here nor created as a simulation instruction, then the Simulation will likely encounter an error. Similarly, if the data type is specified here and required by a Smart Contract, but does not exist in Vault, then the Simulation will likely encounter an error.

account.  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of the Account. Required.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_TYPE\_UNKNOWN:**  
This status exists to avoid an empty request unintentionally setting an undesired type. An Account will never have this type.  
**ACCOUNT\_TYPE\_CUSTOMER:**  
An Account for a Customer of the bank. Customer Accounts are backed by Smart Contracts.  
**ACCOUNT\_TYPE\_INTERNAL:**  
An Account where the bank is the (implicit) stakeholder. Internal Accounts are not backed by Smart Contracts.  
  
**Default**

string

The ID of the Smart Contract Version the Account is currently on.  
  
*For create requests*: This must be set for Customer Accounts, but must be empty for Internal Accounts.  
  
*For update requests*: This can be directly updated to request the converting of a Customer Account to a new Smart Contract version.  
  
Only the hooks on this Smart Contract Version will be executed (supervisors and propagation delays notwithstanding) with the exception of the conversion hook which would be run for the pending Smart Contract Version.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
v2\_create\_account.  
account.  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the Account. When creating an Internal Account this must be set to OPEN. When creating a Customer Account this must be set to either PENDING or OPEN. This can only be updated to OPEN, CLOSED or CANCELLED.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
This status exists to avoid an empty request unintentionally setting an undesired status. An Account will never have this status.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING:**  
An Account that has not been activated. If this status was requested, the PENDING response means that no hook has yet been run, no schedules will exist, and Postings will be rejected. If the OPEN status was requested, a PENDING response means that manual remediation is required. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPENING:**  
An Account in the process of being activated. Its activation hook has been successfully executed but the directives it produced may not have been committed yet. This status is intended to be short-lived; if it persists for any length of time it may indicate that user intervention is required. Vault will continually attempt to move to OPEN status asynchronously. Postings will be rejected unless they come from the activation hook. Any such Postings may have been committed. Schedules may have been created. Notifications may have been sent.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN:**  
An Account has been activated. Postings are accepted based on the presence of any Restrictions, and the Smart Contract behaviour. Schedules have been created and commenced as of the activation time. In the event that Postings and/or notifications failed during the activation process, an error will be returned. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSING:**  
An Account is in the process of being closed. Its deactivation hook has been successfully executed but the resulting postings may not have been committed and schedules may not have been deactivated yet. This status is intended to be short-lived; if it persists for any length of time it may indicate that user intervention is required. Vault will continually attempt to move to CLOSED status asynchronously. Postings are accepted based on the presence of any Restrictions, and the Smart Contract behaviour. Schedules may continue to execute if not yet deactivated.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED:**  
The Account has been closed. Its balances are zero and new postings will be rejected. All schedules have been deactivated, although latent events may still occur (which cannot affect balances). This is a terminal status. Some notifications may not have been successful in the deactivation process if an error was returned. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CANCELLED:**  
The Account is cancelled. No hooks are allowed. No postings are allowed. No schedules exist. This status can only be moved to from PENDING.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_OPENING:**  
The Account is in pending open status.  
Postings will be rejected unless they come from the activation hook. Any such Postings may have been committed. Schedules may have been created. Notifications may have been sent. Once in this status an Account can only move to OPEN.  
DEPRECATED: This status exists to support v1 endpoints on v2 and will be removed no earlier than Vault Core 7.0. The Account is represented as OPEN on v1 endpoints. In v2, the Account may or may not be activated. Activation Account Updates are created which will activate the Account and update it to OPEN once complete.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE:**  
The Account is in pending closure status.  
DEPRECATED: This status exists to support v1 endpoints on v2 and will be removed no earlier than Vault Core 7.0. The closure Account update is created. The closure hook is run. The Account remains in this state until manually updated to closed. Balances are checked when transitioning to CLOSED.  
  
**Default**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN**

 |
|

For more information, see [Important Caveats when running Simulation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contract_simulation#important_caveats_when_running_simulation).  
  
*instructions\[\] items can contain one of create\_account, v2\_create\_account, **create\_posting\_instruction\_batch**, create\_global\_parameter, create\_global\_parameter\_value, create\_flag\_definition, create\_flag, create\_plan, create\_account\_plan\_assoc, create\_account\_update, update\_account, v2\_update\_account, create\_calendar, create\_calendar\_event, create\_smart\_contract\_module\_versions\_link, update\_smart\_contract\_param, create\_parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node, create\_parameter, create\_parameter\_value, update\_parameter\_value, batch\_create\_parameter\_values, create\_processing\_group, update\_processing\_group or list\_account\_attribute\_values*

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_id**  
  
string

 | 

Client Transactions must be unique for a given client ID. Required.  
\- Asynchronous API: Uniquely identifies a client of the Postings API. This must refer to an existing Postings API Client resource, which then determines the Kafka topic to which responses are published.  
\- Synchronous API: See the [Postings documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api#sync-using_the_api) for information about chaining Posting Instruction Batch requests.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_batch\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A correlation ID across different posting instruction batches. This drives no direct behaviour in Vault, but may be used as a filter for listing posting instruction batches. It is also used as the Kafka partition key for responses and events. The suggested use is to set the same `client_batch_id` across batches that contain posting instructions for the same financial transaction. Required.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**posting\_instructions\[\]**  
  
array \[object\]

 | 

A non-empty list of posting instruction objects to be processed atomically. Required.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
**client\_transaction\_id**  
  
string

 | 

Set by the client. This is the ID of the client transaction this posting instruction is creating or mutating. Required.  
  
\-For primary (initiating) posting instructions this must be unique for a given `client_id`  
\-For secondary (subsequent, chained) posting instructions this must refer to a previous `client_transaction_id`

**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for backdated and future-dated instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will be booked. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for back-booked and future-booked instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

instructions\[\].

authorisation\_adjustment.  
**amount**  
  
string

 | 

A delta amount. The sign of the delta can be given explicitly (`"+3.40"`, `"-20"`) or implicitly if it is positive (e.g "3.40" is the same as "+3.40").  
  
*The amount of the AuthorisationAdjustment, which can be specified as a delta (the difference between the previous amount and the new amount) or as a new total authorised amount. On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.  
  
authorisation\_adjustment can contain one of **amount** or replacement\_amount*

 |

On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |

instructions\[\].  
create\_posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**

instructions\[\].  
create\_flag.  
**value**  
  
enum

 | 

Determines how the Flag will behave when resolving the timeseries. Flags with a Value of `FLAG_VALUE_ON` will be resolved as `True`, and a Value of `FLAG_VALUE_OFF` will be resolved as `False`. Defaults to `FLAG_VALUE_ON`. If there are multiple overlapping Flags, the most recently created one will take precendence. If an Account has multiple Stakeholders with conflicting Flags for the same Flag Definition ID, the `FLAG_VALUE_ON` Flag will take precendence.  
  
**Enum values**  
**FLAG\_VALUE\_ON:**  
A Flag with Value `FLAG_VALUE_ON` will be treated as `True` for its effective range when resolving the Flag timeseries.  
**FLAG\_VALUE\_OFF:**  
A Flag with Value `FLAG_VALUE_OFF` will be treated as `False` for its effective range when resolving the Flag timeseries.  
  
**Default**  
**FLAG\_VALUE\_ON**

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_flag.  
**effective\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The timestamp at which the Flag becomes effective, in UTC. For create requests, can be either:  
\- left empty (for a flag effective immediately);  
\- set to a time in the future (to schedule a flag taking effect); or  
\- set to a time in the past (if the `is_backdated` field is set to true).  
Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. Truncated to microsecond precision.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_flag.  
**expiry\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The timestamp at which the Flag stops being effective, in UTC. The Flag is considered effective between `effective_timestamp` and `expiry_timestamp`.  
\- If `expiry_timestamp` is specified, it must be after the `effective_timestamp` time.  
\- If `expiry_timestamp` is not specified, the Flag is considered effective from its `effective_timestamp` onwards.  
Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. Will be truncated to microsecond precision.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
create\_flag.  
**is\_backdated**  
  
boolean

 | 

Indicates whether this Flag was a backdated change, meaning its `effective_timestamp` was set to a time earlier than when it was created. To allow the `effective_timestamp` to be in the past, this must be set to true when creating a Flag. Optional.

This instruction will allow you to close an account on a Smart Contract that references Parameters via the `expected_parameters` [metadata field](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/smart_contracts_api_reference4xx/metadata#expected_parameters) in the Smart Contract. For more information, see [Important Caveats when running Simulation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contract_simulation#important_caveats_when_running_simulation).

 |

 |

instructions\[\].  
update\_account.  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the account. Optional for creation. Valid updates are from ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN or ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CANCELLED, ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE or ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED, ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED. Updating the status to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN will trigger the creation of an account update with an `activation_update` field and run the contract activation code. Updating the status to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE will trigger the creation of an account update with a `closure_update` field and run the contract `deactivation_hook`. Accounts can only be updated from ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED when the `closing_timestamp` is provided, the account has a zero balance, and at least one `activation_update` account update has the status ACCOUNT\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_COMPLETED. Accounts can only be updated from ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED once the `closure_update` account update has the status ACCOUNT\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_COMPLETED and the account has a zero balance. Note that when updating the account from ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE to ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED, a `closing_timestamp` may be provided.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN:**  
Account has been approved and transactions are allowed.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED:**  
Account was previously open but is now permanently closed.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CANCELLED:**  
Account was requested but was never approved, it is now permanently closed.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE:**  
Account was requested closure but contract and account closure are not finished.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING:**  
Account and contract record has been created, it is waiting for another call to be made open.  
  
**Default**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN**

**v2\_update\_account**  
  
object

 | 

Instructs the simulation to update an account with a V2 Account UpdateAccount request. Note that stakeholder IDs and details are not supported in simulation, and cannot be updated. This instruction cannot be used in the same SimulateContractsRequest as create\_account, create\_account\_update or update\_account instructions.  
  
*instructions\[\] items can contain one of create\_account, v2\_create\_account, create\_posting\_instruction\_batch, create\_global\_parameter, create\_global\_parameter\_value, create\_flag\_definition, create\_flag, create\_plan, create\_account\_plan\_assoc, create\_account\_update, update\_account, **v2\_update\_account**, create\_calendar, create\_calendar\_event, create\_smart\_contract\_module\_versions\_link, update\_smart\_contract\_param, create\_parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node, create\_parameter, create\_parameter\_value, update\_parameter\_value, batch\_create\_parameter\_values, create\_processing\_group, update\_processing\_group or list\_account\_attribute\_values*

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
v2\_update\_account.  
**account**  
  
object

 | 

The Account to update. Only the fields being updated need to be specified.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
v2\_update\_account.  
account.  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Account. When creating a customer Account this field is optional and will default to a UUID if not provided. When creating an internal Account this field is required. Max length: 36 characters.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
v2\_update\_account.  
account.  
**smart\_contract\_version\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Smart Contract Version the Account is currently on.  
  
*For create requests*: This must be set for Customer Accounts, but must be empty for Internal Accounts.  
  
*For update requests*: This can be directly updated to request the converting of a Customer Account to a new Smart Contract version.  
  
Only the hooks on this Smart Contract Version will be executed (supervisors and propagation delays notwithstanding) with the exception of the conversion hook which would be run for the pending Smart Contract Version.

 |
| 

instructions\[\].  
v2\_update\_account.  
account.  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the Account. When creating an Internal Account this must be set to OPEN. When creating a Customer Account this must be set to either PENDING or OPEN. This can only be updated to OPEN, CLOSED or CANCELLED.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
This status exists to avoid an empty request unintentionally setting an undesired status. An Account will never have this status.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING:**  
An Account that has not been activated. If this status was requested, the PENDING response means that no hook has yet been run, no schedules will exist, and Postings will be rejected. If the OPEN status was requested, a PENDING response means that manual remediation is required. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPENING:**  
An Account in the process of being activated. Its activation hook has been successfully executed but the directives it produced may not have been committed yet. This status is intended to be short-lived; if it persists for any length of time it may indicate that user intervention is required. Vault will continually attempt to move to OPEN status asynchronously. Postings will be rejected unless they come from the activation hook. Any such Postings may have been committed. Schedules may have been created. Notifications may have been sent.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_OPEN:**  
An Account has been activated. Postings are accepted based on the presence of any Restrictions, and the Smart Contract behaviour. Schedules have been created and commenced as of the activation time. In the event that Postings and/or notifications failed during the activation process, an error will be returned. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSING:**  
An Account is in the process of being closed. Its deactivation hook has been successfully executed but the resulting postings may not have been committed and schedules may not have been deactivated yet. This status is intended to be short-lived; if it persists for any length of time it may indicate that user intervention is required. Vault will continually attempt to move to CLOSED status asynchronously. Postings are accepted based on the presence of any Restrictions, and the Smart Contract behaviour. Schedules may continue to execute if not yet deactivated.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CLOSED:**  
The Account has been closed. Its balances are zero and new postings will be rejected. All schedules have been deactivated, although latent events may still occur (which cannot affect balances). This is a terminal status. Some notifications may not have been successful in the deactivation process if an error was returned. For more information, see [Troubleshooting Customer Accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/accounts/accounts_version_2#troubleshooting_customer_accounts).  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_CANCELLED:**  
The Account is cancelled. No hooks are allowed. No postings are allowed. No schedules exist. This status can only be moved to from PENDING.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_OPENING:**  
The Account is in pending open status.  
Postings will be rejected unless they come from the activation hook. Any such Postings may have been committed. Schedules may have been created. Notifications may have been sent. Once in this status an Account can only move to OPEN.  
DEPRECATED: This status exists to support v1 endpoints on v2 and will be removed no earlier than Vault Core 7.0. The Account is represented as OPEN on v1 endpoints. In v2, the Account may or may not be activated. Activation Account Updates are created which will activate the Account and update it to OPEN once complete.  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_PENDING\_CLOSURE:**  
The Account is in pending closure status.  
DEPRECATED: This status exists to support v1 endpoints on v2 and will be removed no earlier than Vault Core 7.0. The closure Account update is created. The closure hook is run. The Account remains in this state until manually updated to closed. Balances are checked when transitioning to CLOSED.  
  
**Default**  
**ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN**

instructions\[\].  
update\_parameter\_value.  
effective\_to\_timestamp\_update\_options.  
**set\_to\_now**  
  
boolean

 | 

This controls the behaviour when a request is sent to update the `effective_to_timestamp` but no value is set in `parameter_value.effective_to_timestamp`. When set to true, Vault immediately unsets the Parameter Value by setting its `effective_to_timestamp` to the time that Vault processes the request. This is an alternative to explicitly setting a near-future `effective_to_timestamp`, which could inadvertently be in the past by the time of processing. When set to false, or if this update option is omitted, the `effective_to_timestamp` will be left unbounded or set to the `effective_from_timestamp` of the next Parameter Value in the timeseries.

**internal\_account\_processing\_label**

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.

 |

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].

**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
An OutboundAuthorisation, InboundAuthorisation, Transfer, OutboundHardSettlement or InboundHardSettlement specifies a `client_transaction_id` which already exists in the namespace of the `client_id`.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_DOES\_NOT\_EXIST:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment, Settlement, Release is referring to a non existent client transaction.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_ADJUSTMENT\_YIELDS\_AUTHORISATION\_WITH\_NEGATIVE\_AMOUNT:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment yields an authorisation with a negative amount.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_CLOSED:**  
An instruction is attempting to mutate a client transaction that has been closed.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_INVALID\_OPERATION:**  
An instruction is being added to a client transaction where the `value_timestamp` is not strictly later than the current latest instruction, or the instruction being processed would create a client transaction which has a combination of CustomInstructions and other instruction types.

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
account\_violations\[\].  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_ACCOUNT\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s target account is not present.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s target account is in a status that doesn’t allow postings (for example: CLOSED, or PENDING).  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_UNSUPPORTED\_DENOMINATION:**  
The instruction’s target account does not support the posted denomination.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_PAYMENT\_DEVICE\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s payment device token resolved to a payment device that has an invalid status as of this batch’s value\_timestamp.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_MULTIPLE\_PROCESSING\_GROUPS:**  
The instruction affects multiple accounts that do not all share the same processing group.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_INTERNAL\_ACCOUNT\_PROCESSING\_LABEL\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s internal account processing label is not present.

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
restriction\_violations\[\].  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of restriction violation. For instructions instructed prior to Vault version 5.4, this will be returned as `RESTRICTION_VIOLATION_TYPE_UNKNOWN`.  
  
**Enum values**  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_UNKNOWN:**  
An unknown restriction type.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_PREVENT\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which prevents credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_PREVENT\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which prevents debits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_REVIEW\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which requires reviewing credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_REVIEW\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which requires reviewing debits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_LIMIT\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which limits credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_LIMIT\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which limits debits.

*A more accurate violation type is now provided in violation\_type*

The Posting instruction cannot be applied due to insufficient funds.

contract\_violations\[\].  
**violation\_type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of contract violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_VIOLATION\_UNKNOWN:**  
The contract execution violation type is unknown.  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_VIOLATION\_BREACH\_TERMS\_AND\_CONDITIONS:**  
The instruction breaches the terms and conditions of the target account’s contract.  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_VIOLATION\_INSUFFICIENT\_FUNDS:**  
The instruction cannot be applied due to insufficient funds.  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_VIOLATION\_WRONG\_DENOMINATION:**

**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_CUSTOM\_REASON:**

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].

**booking\_localised\_date\_time**  
  
string

 | 

An RFC 3339 compliant date/time string representing the `booking_timestamp` of the PostingInstructionBatch, localised into the time zone of the processing group associated with accounts referenced in this PostingInstruction. As the processing group may change over time, this field will not be populated for future-booked postings.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for backdated and future-dated instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will be booked. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for back-booked and future-booked instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

 |

dateTime

posting\_instructions\[\].  
**source\_insertion\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

Specifies the time the posting instruction was inserted in the source core banking engine. Will always have the same value as `insertion_timestamp` unless posting instruction was migrated into Vault via the Posting Migration API.

A delta amount. The sign of the delta can be given explicitly (`"+3.40"`, `"-20"`) or implicitly if it is positive (e.g "3.40" is the same as "+3.40").  
  
*The amount of the AuthorisationAdjustment, which can be specified as a delta (the difference between the previous amount and the new amount) or as a new total authorised amount. On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.

On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.

**POSTING\_PHASE\_PENDING\_INCOMING:**

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
custom\_instruction.  
postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**batch\_details**  
  
map \[string: string\]

 | 

Stores metadata related to the posting instruction batch resource. These details can also be retrieved in the posting instruction resource. Optional.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the processing of the posting instruction batch.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_ACCEPTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been accepted and Postings have been committed to the ledger.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been rejected and no Postings have been committed to the ledger.

 |

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
error.  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of error returned.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest contains invalid arguments and the request cannot be processed. See the error message for more details. Cannot Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INTERNAL:**  
An internal error occurred due to unexpected condition while processing the request. Can Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_TTL\_EXPIRED:**  
A time to live expiry error occured because the requested `time_to_live` timestamp has expired. Cannot Retry.

It is also used as the Kafka partition key for responses and events. The suggested use is to set the same `client_batch_id` across batches that contain posting instructions for the same financial transaction. Required.

posting\_instruction\_batch\_created\_events\[\].

posting\_instructions\[\].  
committed\_postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |

 | 

Captures rejection reasons caused by posting logic validity checks. For example: Cannot adjust an authorisation that has already been settled.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch\_created\_events\[\].  
posting\_instruction\_batch.  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
posting\_violations\[\].  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
An OutboundAuthorisation, InboundAuthorisation, Transfer, OutboundHardSettlement or InboundHardSettlement specifies a `client_transaction_id` which already exists in the namespace of the `client_id`.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_DOES\_NOT\_EXIST:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment, Settlement, Release is referring to a non existent client transaction.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_ADJUSTMENT\_YIELDS\_AUTHORISATION\_WITH\_NEGATIVE\_AMOUNT:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment yields an authorisation with a negative amount.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_CLOSED:**  
An instruction is attempting to mutate a client transaction that has been closed.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_INVALID\_OPERATION:**  
An instruction is being added to a client transaction where the `value_timestamp` is not strictly later than the current latest instruction, or the instruction being processed would create a client transaction which has a combination of CustomInstructions and other instruction types.

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_ACCOUNT\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s target account is not present.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s target account is in a status that doesn’t allow postings (for example: CLOSED, or PENDING).  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_UNSUPPORTED\_DENOMINATION:**  
The instruction’s target account does not support the posted denomination.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_PAYMENT\_DEVICE\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s payment device token resolved to a payment device that has an invalid status as of this batch’s value\_timestamp.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_MULTIPLE\_PROCESSING\_GROUPS:**  
The instruction affects multiple accounts that do not all share the same processing group.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_INTERNAL\_ACCOUNT\_PROCESSING\_LABEL\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s internal account processing label is not present.
