#### [](#_core_api_v1_parameters_BatchCreateParameterValuesResponse_BatchCreateParameterValues "Copy link to heading")BatchCreate

Changes the values of several Parameters for a single owner at a particular point in time; this includes replacing any empty fields (None) with values. The batch request is atomic; if an individual request in the batch fails, then the whole request will fail with no side-effects. All values in the batch must have the same `effective_from_timestamp`.  
  
If the owner of the Parameter Values is an Account, then the [pre\_parameter\_change\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/smart_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#pre_parameter_change_hook) and [post\_parameter\_change\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/smart_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#post_parameter_change_hook) will run for an `INSTANCE` level `Parameter`, or an [ExpectedParameter](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/common_types_4xx/classes#ExpectedParameter) which has opted in to the hooks.  
These hooks are not run for Customer Accounts that are not yet OPEN, or if the Parameter Value is backdated.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.parameter\_values:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/parameter-values:batchCreate

#### [](#_core_api_v1_parameters_BatchGetParameterValuesResponse_BatchGetParameterValues "Copy link to heading")BatchGet

Retrieves one or more Parameter Values by their IDs.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.parameter\_values:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/parameter-values:batchGet

##### [](#request_111 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

IDs of Parameter Values to retrieve. Maximum 100. Required.

 |

##### [](#responses_51 "Copy link to heading")Responses

Success Errors

Response fields  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**parameter\_values**  
  
map \[string: object\]

 | 

Parameter Values keyed on ID.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

Unique UUID identifier for the Parameter Value. Read-only and set to a random UUID on creation when using `POST /v1/parameter-values`. When using `POST /v1/contracts:simulate` it can optionally be specified in the request to allow the Parameter Value to be updated later in the simulation.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**parameter\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Parameter for which this is a value. Required.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**account\_config\_group\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Account Config Group that owns this value. Can only be set to `root`, and is exactly equivalent to setting `global` to `true`. Functionality originally intended for this field has now moved to `parameter_value_hierarchy_node_id`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.3**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by `global`. Prior to removal of this field, if this field is populated it will be set to `root`, and `global` will also be set to `true`.*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**value**  
  
object

 | 

The value of the Parameter, which must satisfy the constraints defined in the Parameter. Required. Cannot be changed; instead, a new Parameter Value must be created.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
value.  
**string\_value**  
  
string

 | 

The value of a string Parameter.  
  
*The value of the Parameter.  
  
value can contain one of **string\_value**, decimal\_value, enumeration\_value, date\_time\_value or account\_id\_value*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
value.  
**decimal\_value**  
  
string

 | 

The value of a decimal Parameter.  
  
*The value of the Parameter.  
  
value can contain one of string\_value, **decimal\_value**, enumeration\_value, date\_time\_value or account\_id\_value*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
value.  
**enumeration\_value**  
  
string

 | 

The value of an enumeration Parameter.  
  
*The value of the Parameter.  
  
value can contain one of string\_value, decimal\_value, **enumeration\_value**, date\_time\_value or account\_id\_value*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
value.  
**date\_time\_value**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The value of a date-time Parameter, in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.  
  
*The value of the Parameter.  
  
value can contain one of string\_value, decimal\_value, enumeration\_value, **date\_time\_value** or account\_id\_value*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
value.  
**account\_id\_value**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of an Account, may be Internal or Customer.  
  
*The value of the Parameter.  
  
value can contain one of string\_value, decimal\_value, enumeration\_value, date\_time\_value or **account\_id\_value***

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**effective\_from\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The time from which the Parameter Value is effective (including this time), in UTC. Set to the current time on creation if not specified. Can be set to a time in the past if the `is_backdated` flag is set to true. Can also be set to a time in the future: see [Future-Dated Parameter Values](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/common_examples/generic#future_dated_parameter_values). Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. Will be truncated to microsecond precision.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**effective\_to\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The time until which the Parameter Value remains effective (excluding this time), in UTC. If this field is left empty or omitted, the Parameter Value is effective indefinitely. Vault will automatically update this field if the Parameter Value is superseded by another Parameter Value for the same Parameter and Owner. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. Will be truncated to microsecond precision.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**effective\_to\_timestamp\_is\_explicit**  
  
boolean

 | 

Indicates whether the `effective_to_timestamp` was set explicitly using an API call or whether it was implicitly determined by Vault as a result of another Parameter Value for the same Owner superseding it. Read-only.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**is\_backdated**  
  
boolean

 | 

Indicates whether this Parameter Value was a backdated change, meaning its `effective_from_timestamp` was set to a time earlier than when it was created. To allow the `effective_from_timestamp` to be in the past, this must be set to true when creating Parameter Values. A backdated Parameter Value will not trigger the [pre\_parameter\_change\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/smart_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#pre_parameter_change_hook) or [post\_parameter\_change\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/smart_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#post_parameter_change_hook).

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**is\_cancelled**  
  
boolean

 | 

Indicates whether this Parameter Value has been cancelled before it became effective. This field can be explicitly set to true via an update, providing that the `effective_from_timestamp` is in the future.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**cancel\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The time at which this Parameter Value was cancelled, in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**create\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The time that the Parameter Value was created, in UTC. Read-only and set to the current time on creation. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**update\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The time that the Parameter Value was last updated, in UTC. Empty if the Value was never updated. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**account\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Customer Account that owns this value.  
  
*parameter\_values\[KEY\] can contain one of **account\_id**, global or parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node\_id*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**global**  
  
boolean

 | 

Whether or not this Parameter Value is globally owned. This field should be used instead of account\_config\_group\_id='root'. All Resources will use this value unless it’s overridden by a Parameter Value owned by a hierarchy or the Resource itself.  
  
*parameter\_values\[KEY\] can contain one of account\_id, **global** or parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node\_id*

 |
| 

parameter\_values\[KEY\].  
**parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Parameter Value Hierarchy Node that owns this value. Required for create requests.  
  
*parameter\_values\[KEY\] can contain one of account\_id, global or **parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node\_id***

 |

#### [](#available_methods_46 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

#### [](#_core_api_v1_parameters_ListParameterValueHierarchyNodesResponse_ListParameterValueHierarchyNodes "Copy link to heading")List

Retrieves a filtered and paginated list of Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes.  
\- To obtain the entire hierarchy, specify no filters.  
\- To obtain only the first layer of nodes, stop paging once a node of depth 2 is reached.  
\- Subtrees within the hierarchy can be traversed using the `parent_ids` filter.  
\- The `names` filter can be used to find nodes by their more human-friendly names. It can be combined with the `parent_ids` filter to find nodes with a particular name within a subtree of the hierarchy. Names are unique among siblings, so filtering on a single name and parent ID will return at most one result.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_nodes:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Page Level

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/parameter-value-hierarchy-nodes

##### [](#request_112 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes to be returned. Maximum 100. Required.

 |
| 

**page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The token of the requested page, which comes from a previous GET v1/parameter-value-hierarchy-nodes response. All other fields of the request must be kept the same as the request which resulted in the page token. If empty, the first page will be returned.

 |
| 

**order\_by**  
  
enum

 | 

The order in which Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes will be returned. When ordering results with the same value, Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes will be sorted by ascending `parent_id` and then by ascending `id`.  
  
**Enum values**  
**ORDER\_BY\_DEPTH\_ASC**  
  
**Default**  
**ORDER\_BY\_DEPTH\_ASC**

 |
| 

**parent\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

A set of Parameter Value Hierarchy Node IDs. Matches all Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes with a `parent_id` in the set. Must not contain empty IDs.

 |
| 

**names**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

A set of names. Matches all Parameter Value Hierarchy Nodes with a `name` in the provided names. Must not contain empty strings.

 |

#### [](#_core_api_v1_parameters_ParameterValueHierarchyNode_UpdateParameterValueHierarchyNode "Copy link to heading")Update

Updates a Parameter Value Hierarchy Node.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_nodes:write

**Endpoint:** PUT /v1/parameter-value-hierarchy-nodes/{parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node.id}

##### [](#request_114 "Copy link to heading")Request

Path parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node.  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

Unique identifier for the Parameter Value Hierarchy Node. Forms part of the `parent_path` for child nodes. Thought Machine recommends against relating this to the `name` (instead it can a good idea to use the id to indicate this node’s position). It must match the regex `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-_.]*$` and its length must not exceed 256 characters. Required for create or update requests.

 |

Body parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**request\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A unique ID used to ensure this request is idempotent.

 |
| 

**parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node**  
  
object

 | 

The Parameter Value Hierarchy Node to update. Required.

 |
| 

parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node.  
**name**  
  
string

 | 

A human readable identifier for this Parameter Value Hierarchy Node. It must match the regex `^[A-Za-z0-9][ A-Za-z0-9-_]*$` and its length must not exceed 256 characters. The `name` needs to be unique among nodes with a common (or no) `parent_id`. Required for create requests.

 |
| 

parameter\_value\_hierarchy\_node.  
**metadata**  
  
map \[string: string\]

 | 

Key value map of additional, non-structured Parameter Value Hierarchy Node details.  
  
The details must not include:  
\- Any image data, including any KYC collateral such as passport, licence or other images. These must be stored in a separate repository outside of Vault.  
\- Any data that is classified as PII data.  
The details cannot be utilised by Smart Contracts to drive any type of product behaviour.  
  
Max size: 2kB, Max key length: 128 characters

 |
| 

**update\_mask**  
  
object

 | 

The paths of the resource to update. Values will be taken from the `parameter_value_hierarchy_node` field. The only allowed fields are `name` and `metadata`. Metadata entries can be removed by specifying a key with an empty value. Keys with values will create new entries or replace existing ones. Any existing entries with keys not in the request will not be modified. Required.

 |
| 

update\_mask.  
**paths\[\]**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

The set of field mask paths.

## [](#payment_devices "Copy link to heading")Payment devices

Payment devices are Vault’s generic mechanism to represent instruments that can receive and initiate Postings. A PaymentDevice is generic because the payment schemes they are used for vary greatly between Vault instances.

### [](#paymentdevice "Copy link to heading")PaymentDevice

A **PaymentDevice** has an ID and an unstructured `routing_info` field, to which core Vault is agnostic. They are not tied to any **Account** or customer and are usually created for referential purposes by an upper payment integration layer. Card PAN number, IBAN, UK **Account** number and sort code, phone number, email are all examples of what a payment device might refer to in a Vault instance, depending on what is available for payment routing.

### [](#paymentdevicelinks "Copy link to heading")PaymentDeviceLinks

**PaymentDeviceLinks** associate Vault **Accounts** with **PaymentDevices** in order to receive or initiate Postings. They are created with IDs referencing those two resources and from that point onwards can only become inactive. A payment device can be linked to multiple Accounts and an **Account** can be linked to multiple payment devices. At the same time, the same **Account** and payment device can be associated using multiple **PaymentDeviceLinks**.

This is useful when for example, the same card uses multiple **Accounts** and has some business logic based on denomination plus other factors applied or when an **Account** receives payments via a card, email, phone number at the same time. It is up to the business layer to decide which **PaymentDeviceLink** to use for both inbound and outbound Postings. It’s usually a combination of custom business logic and customer input.

### [](#paymentdevicetokens "Copy link to heading")PaymentDeviceTokens

To make **Account** resolution for Inbound Postings more performant, each link is associated with a **PaymentDeviceToken**, hence avoiding to search through **PaymentDeviceLinks**. The **PaymentDeviceToken** can be a hash of the PAN number or the PAN number combined with custom business logic, such as denomination, country, and so on.

For example: Inbound Postings usually have to be performed under strict SLAs depending on the payment scheme they use. The Posting object accepts this field when a request is created and will either use it to resolve the **Account** or fail if no **PaymentDeviceLink** is associated with it.

Because the Posting **Account** resolution has to happen to exactly one **Account**, the token must be unique across all active PaymentDeviceLinks. If the business logic changes, for example when a customer wants their card to draw money from a different **Account**, the **PaymentDeviceLink** with the PaymentDeviceToken can be made inactive and a new **PaymentDeviceLink** associating the same PaymentDevice with a new **Account** can be created using the same token. This way, **Account** resolution for payments remains fast even if requirements change. In practice, it is quite useful to think of the lifetime of a token as the disjoint time intervals of **PaymentDeviceLinks** that it was associated with.

### [](#paymentdevice_2 "Copy link to heading")PaymentDevice

## [](#plans "Copy link to heading")Plans

Plans are Vault’s mechanism for grouping [accounts](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#accounts) together under one Supervisor Contract. This lets you share logic between accounts and handle operations for a group of accounts.

For more information about the features relating to Plans in Vault, see the [Plans](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/plans/) reference section.

### [](#creating_a_plan "Copy link to heading")Creating a Plan

When a Plan is created, it must have an associated Supervisor Contract version. The Supervisor Contract version ID is immutable.

The schedules specified in the Supervisor Contract version are active when a Plan is created and an activation Plan update for the Plan is completed.

### [](#supervisor_contract_versions "Copy link to heading")Supervisor Contract versions

A Plan is always powered by an underlying [Supervisor Contract version](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#supervisorcontractversion). A Supervisor Contract version dictates the Plan’s behaviour.

### [](#associating_and_disassociating_accounts_with_plans "Copy link to heading")Associating and disassociating accounts with Plans

Accounts can be associated and disassociated with Plans via [Plan updates](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#planupdate). An account can only be associated with at most one Plan at any given moment. Association is only allowed for both OPEN Plans and accounts.

The status of account Plan associations can be checked via [account plan associations](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#accountplanassoc).

### [](#plan_updates "Copy link to heading")Plan updates

Plan updates are used to perform asynchronous mutations on the Plan, such as:

-   Activating a Plan
    
-   Closing a Plan
    
-   Associating an account with a Plan
    
-   Disassociating an account from a Plan
    
-   Updating the Supervisor Contract version of a Plan
    

When a Plan is created with status `PLAN_STATUS_OPEN`, an activation Plan update is created automatically.

### [](#storing_dynamic_data "Copy link to heading")Storing dynamic data

Any dynamic data that a Vault instance needs to store against the Plan can be put in the `details` field and referenced later during custom processes. Vault is agnostic to what is stored in the `details` field.

### [](#accountplanassoc "Copy link to heading")AccountPlanAssoc

| 

plan\_migrations\[\].  
supervisor\_contract\_version\_migration.  
**schedule\_migration\_type**  
  
enum

 | 

Specifies how existing schedules should be migrated.  
  
Note: This field has no effect on migrations to a Supervisor Contract version on Contracts Language API version 4.  
[See Plan migrations.](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/plans#plan_migrations)  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **4.6**, and will be removed no earlier than release **6.0**  
*This field is not used on updates to Contracts Language API version 4 and will be removed alongside Contracts Language API version 3.*  
  
**Enum values**  
**SCHEDULE\_MIGRATION\_TYPE\_RECREATE\_ALL\_SCHEDULES\_AND\_GROUPS:**  
When updating the Supervisor Contract version of a Plan, all existing schedules will be deleted then recreated according to the Supervisor Contract code of the new product version. Any updates previously made to existing schedules will not be preserved. This is the default behaviour.  
**SCHEDULE\_MIGRATION\_TYPE\_PRESERVE\_SCHEDULES\_IF\_NO\_GROUP\_CHANGES:**  
When updating the Supervisor Contract version of a Plan, existing schedules are preserved if either: - They are not part of a group and a schedule of the same event type is defined in the new Supervisor Contract code; or  
\- They are part of a group and a group of the same name, size and order is defined in the new Supervisor Contract code. New schedules are only created if they are defined in the new Supervisor Contract code.

 |
| 

**previous\_page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

Token used to retrieve the previous page. If empty, the response contains the first page of results.

 |
| 

**next\_page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

Token used to retrieve the next page. If empty, the response contains the last page of results.

 |

#### [](#_core_api_v1_plans_ListPlanSchedulesResponse_ListPlanSchedules "Copy link to heading")List

Retrieves Plan Schedules using the provided filters.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.plan\_schedules:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Best Effort

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/plan-schedules

##### [](#request_131 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**plan\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The Plan ID that Plan Schedules are to be listed for. Required; must be non-empty.

 |
| 

**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of results to be retrieved. Required.  
  
Required.  
Min value: 1.  
Max value: 20.

 |
| 

**page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The token of the page the results are to be retrieved from. If empty, the first page of results will be returned. Optional.

 |
| 

**include\_disassociated**  
  
boolean

 | 

A boolean controlling the Plan Schedules that are returned. When set to `false`, only associated Plan Schedules, that is, Plan Schedules with `is_associated=true`, are returned. When set to `true`, associated and disassociated Plan Schedules are returned. An optional field. False by default.

 |

##### [](#response_76 "Copy link to heading")Response

Response fields  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**plan\_schedules\[\]**  
  
array \[object\]

 | 

A list of matching Plan Schedules, ordered by ascending `create_timestamp` then by ascending `id`. Note: By default, only associated Plan Schedules are returned. The set of associated Plan Schedules forms a view of the current state of the Event Types for the Plan. To view plan schedules that are no longer associated, for example, after the contract directive `update_event_type` is executed, set `include_disassociated` to `true` to return disassociated plan schedules.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Plan Schedule.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**plan\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The Plan ID associated with the Plan Schedule.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**name**  
  
string

 | 

The name of the Plan Schedule.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**group\_name**  
  
string

 | 

The name of the group associated with the Plan Schedule.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**time\_expression**  
  
string

 | 

The expression that defines when Jobs will be run. This can be either a cron expression or a schedule method (e.g. `EndOfMonthSchedule`). The syntax for cron expressions follows [https://github.com/thought-machine/cronexpr](https://github.com/thought-machine/cronexpr) (to be used strictly for interpreting cron syntax). For constructing expressions, please refer to the smart contract documentation.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**schedule\_tag\_ids\[\]**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

The schedule tag IDs for a given Plan Schedule.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**create\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

The timestamp of when this Plan Schedule was created, in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp. Note: this is different from the create timestamp of the Schedule with the same ID.

 |
| 

plan\_schedules\[\].  
**is\_associated**  
  
boolean

 | 

A value used to indicate the operational relevance of the Plan Schedule to the Plan. An associated Plan Schedule (where `is_associated` is true); typically references a non-disabled Schedule (one that is not in `SCHEDULE_STATUS_DISABLED`). A disassociated Plan Schedule typically references a disabled Schedule (one that is in `SCHEDULE_STATUS_DISABLED`). There is one associated Plan Schedule per event type in the Supervisor Contract version.

 |
| 

**previous\_page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The pagination token used to retrieve the previous page. If empty, this is the first page of results.

 |
| 

**next\_page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The pagination token used to retrieve the next page. If empty, this is the last page of results.

 |

Retrieves Plan updates using the provided filters.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.plan\_updates:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Best Effort

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/plan-updates

##### [](#request_132 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**plan\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

The IDs of Plans that Plan Updates are to be listed for. At least one of plan\_ids and job\_ids is required; must be non-empty.

 |
| 

**job\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

IDs of the jobs that Plan Updates are to be listed for. At least one of plan\_ids and job\_ids is required.

 |

**statuses**  
  
array \[enum\]

 | 

The statuses of Plan Updates to filter on. Optional.  
  
**Enum values**  
**PLAN\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**PLAN\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_PENDING\_EXECUTION:**  
The Plan Update has not been picked up from the queue yet, or is in progress.  
**PLAN\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_COMPLETED:**  
The Plan Update was successfully executed.  
**PLAN\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The Plan Update failed validation and has been rejected.  
**PLAN\_UPDATE\_STATUS\_ERRORED:**  
The Plan Update errored.

 |
|

integer

The number of results to be retrieved. Required.

string

supervisor\_contract\_version\_update.  
**schedule\_migration\_type**  
  
enum

 | 

Specifies how existing schedules should be migrated.  
  
Note: This field has no effect on migrations to a Supervisor Contract version on Contracts Language API version 4.  
[See Plan migrations.](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/plans#plan_migrations)  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **4.6**, and will be removed no earlier than release **6.0**  
*This field is not used on updates to Contracts Language API version 4 and will be removed alongside Contracts Language API version 3.*  
  
**Enum values**  
**SCHEDULE\_MIGRATION\_TYPE\_RECREATE\_ALL\_SCHEDULES\_AND\_GROUPS:**  
When updating the Supervisor Contract version of a Plan, all existing schedules will be deleted then recreated according to the Supervisor Contract code of the new product version. Any updates previously made to existing schedules will not be preserved. This is the default behaviour.  
**SCHEDULE\_MIGRATION\_TYPE\_PRESERVE\_SCHEDULES\_IF\_NO\_GROUP\_CHANGES:**  
When updating the Supervisor Contract version of a Plan, existing schedules are preserved if either: - They are not part of a group and a schedule of the same event type is defined in the new Supervisor Contract code; or  
\- They are part of a group and a group of the same name, size and order is defined in the new Supervisor Contract code. New schedules are only created if they are defined in the new Supervisor Contract code.  
  
**Default**  
**SCHEDULE\_MIGRATION\_TYPE\_RECREATE\_ALL\_SCHEDULES\_AND\_GROUPS**

## [](#policy_management "Copy link to heading")Policy Management

### [](#policy "Copy link to heading")Policy

#### [](#available_methods_54 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_policy_management_ListPoliciesResponse_ListPolicies) Lists and filters Policy objects.
    
-   [Create](#_core_api_v1_policy_management_Policy_CreatePolicy) Creates a new Policy.
    
-   [Get](#_core_api_v1_policy_management_Policy_GetPolicy) Retrieves a Policy based on a Policy ID.
    
-   [Update](#_core_api_v1_policy_management_Policy_UpdatePolicy) Updates an existing Policy.
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_policy_management_BatchGetPoliciesResponse_BatchGetPolicies) Retrieves one or more Policies based on a list of IDs.

## [](#post_posting_republisher "Copy link to heading")Post Posting Republisher

The Post-Posting Republisher provides functionality to access, delete and republish `post_posting_hook` failures for one or more accounts or plans. Handle these endpoints with care, and be fully aware of their functionality before republishing or deleting Post-Posting Failures. Using these endpoints incorrectly could lead to missing hook directives, potentially affecting the financial state of the accounts.

### [](#postpostingfailure "Copy link to heading")PostPostingFailure

#### [](#available_methods_55 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_ListPostPostingFailuresResponse_ListPostPostingFailures) Lists and filters Post-Posting Failures that are currently stored.
    
-   [Delete](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_DeletePostPostingFailureResponse_DeletePostPostingFailure) DeletePostPostingFailure deletes the Post-Posting Failure.
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_BatchGetPostPostingFailuresResponse_BatchGetPostPostingFailures) Gets one or more Post-Posting Failures based on their ID.
    
-   [Republish](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_PostPostingFailure_RepublishPostPostingFailure) RepublishPostPostingFailure republishes the earliest Post-Posting Failure for an account.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_ListPostPostingFailuresResponse_ListPostPostingFailures "Copy link to heading")List

Lists and filters Post-Posting Failures that are currently stored.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.post\_posting\_failures:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Best Effort

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/post-posting-failures

##### [](#request_140 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**account\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

Filters Post-Posting Failures by the account IDs of their associated failures. Optional.

 |
| 

**posting\_instruction\_batch\_ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

Filters Post-Posting Failures by the posting instruction batch IDs of their associated failures. Optional.

 |
| 

**page\_size**  
  
integer

 | 

The number of Post-Posting Failures to be retrieved.  
  
Required.  
Min value: 1.  
Max value: 50.

 |
| 

**page\_token**  
  
string

 | 

The token of the page the results are to be retrieved from. If empty, this returns the first page of results.

 |
| 

**post\_posting\_failure\_statuses**  
  
array \[enum\]

 | 

Filters Post Posting Failures by the provided failure status. Optional.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_FAILURE:**  
Indicates the Post-Posting Failure was created after a `post_posting_hook` execution was attempted and failed.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_BUFFERED:**  
Indicates this is a Post-Posting execution that has never been attempted because it was blocked by a previous failure.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_PUBLISHED:**  
Indicates this is a republished Post-Posting event and is currently being processed asynchronously.

 |

##### [](#responses_61 "Copy link to heading")Responses

Success Errors

| Name | Description |

array \[object\]

 |

 |
|

**id**  
  
string

 | 

A unique, service-generated UUID.

 |
|

string

 |

 |
|

integer

A counter describing the number of times the Post-Posting Failure has been republished by the user. It starts at 0.

 |
| 

post\_posting\_failures\[\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the Post-Posting Failure.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_FAILURE:**  
Indicates the Post-Posting Failure was created after a `post_posting_hook` execution was attempted and failed.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_BUFFERED:**  
Indicates this is a Post-Posting execution that has never been attempted because it was blocked by a previous failure.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_PUBLISHED:**  
Indicates this is a republished Post-Posting event and is currently being processed asynchronously.

 |

#### [](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_DeletePostPostingFailureResponse_DeletePostPostingFailure "Copy link to heading")Delete

DeletePostPostingFailure deletes the Post-Posting Failure. It will reject requests to delete a Post-Posting Failure that is not the earliest for an account.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.post\_posting\_failures:write

**Endpoint:** DELETE /v1/post-posting-failures/{id}

##### [](#request_141 "Copy link to heading")Request

Path parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the Post-Posting Failure to delete. If the ID is not the earliest for the associated account, the request will be rejected. Required.

 |

 |

#### [](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_BatchGetPostPostingFailuresResponse_BatchGetPostPostingFailures "Copy link to heading")BatchGet

Gets one or more Post-Posting Failures based on their ID.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.post\_posting\_failures:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/post-posting-failures:batchGet

##### [](#request_142 "Copy link to heading")Request

Query parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**ids**  
  
array \[string\]

 | 

A list of IDs of Post-Posting Failures to be retrieved. Required.  
  
Required.  
Min count: 1.  
Max count: 50.

 |

##### [](#responses_63 "Copy link to heading")Responses

Success Errors

Response fields  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**post\_posting\_failures**  
  
map \[string: object\]

 | 

A map of Post-Posting Failure ID to Post-Posting Failures.

 |
| 

post\_posting\_failures\[KEY\].  
**id**  
  
string

 | 

A unique, service-generated UUID.

 |
| 

post\_posting\_failures\[KEY\].

string

 | 

The ID of the Posting Instruction Batch that triggered the failed `post_posting_hook` execution.

 |
| 

post\_posting\_failures\[KEY\].  
**attempt\_number**  
  
integer

 | 

A counter describing the number of times the Post-Posting Failure has been republished by the user. It starts at 0.

 |
| 

post\_posting\_failures\[KEY\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the Post-Posting Failure.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_FAILURE:**  
Indicates the Post-Posting Failure was created after a `post_posting_hook` execution was attempted and failed.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_BUFFERED:**  
Indicates this is a Post-Posting execution that has never been attempted because it was blocked by a previous failure.  
**POST\_POSTING\_FAILURE\_STATUS\_PUBLISHED:**  
Indicates this is a republished Post-Posting event and is currently being processed asynchronously.

string

dateTime

string

 |

string

#### [](#_core_api_v1_post_posting_republisher_PostPostingFailure_RepublishPostPostingFailure "Copy link to heading")Republish

RepublishPostPostingFailure republishes the earliest Post-Posting Failure for an account. It can also republish all blocked failures for the account at the same time.

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.post\_posting\_failures:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/post-posting-failures:republish

##### [](#request_143 "Copy link to heading")Request

Body parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**republish\_type**  
  
enum

 | 

Chosen Republish Type. Defaults to `REPUBLISH_TYPE_REPUBLISH_SINGLE_FAILURE`.  
  
**Enum values**  
**REPUBLISH\_TYPE\_REPUBLISH\_UNKNOWN:**  
Unknown Republish type.  
**REPUBLISH\_TYPE\_REPUBLISH\_SINGLE\_FAILURE:**  
Republishes the earliest Post-Posting Failure that exists for the account or plan.  
**REPUBLISH\_TYPE\_REPUBLISH\_BLOCKED\_FAILURES:**  
Republishes the earliest Post-Posting Failure for the account or plan, as well as all subsequent `post_posting_hook` executions blocked by the failed Post-Posting execution.  
  
**Default**  
**REPUBLISH\_TYPE\_REPUBLISH\_UNKNOWN**

 |
| 

**contract\_execution\_behaviour**  
  
enum

 | 

The behaviour of Smart Contract execution for the republished execution.  
  
**Enum values**  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_BEHAVIOUR\_UNKNOWN:**  
Unknown defaults to Newest.  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_BEHAVIOUR\_NEWEST\_CONTEXT:**  
Newest Context fetch the current execution context before execution.  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_BEHAVIOUR\_RECORDED\_CONTEXT:**  
Recorded context use the context recorded in the db for execution.  
  
**Default**  
**CONTRACT\_EXECUTION\_BEHAVIOUR\_UNKNOWN**

 |
| 

**account\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The account ID to republish an associated Post-Posting Failure for.  
  
*This can contain one of **account\_id** or plan\_id*

 |
| 

**plan\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The plan ID to republish an associated Post-Posting Failure for.  
  
*This can contain one of account\_id or **plan\_id***

 |

## [](#posting_instruction_batches "Copy link to heading")Posting instruction batches

Use the Posting Instruction Batches resource to create synchronous high priority Posting Instruction Batches in production (via `POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches`), to query Posting Instruction Batches, or to create asynchronous Posting Instruction Batches in a test environment (via `POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches:asyncCreate`). There is also a Kafka-based asynchronous API, used for low-priority Postings in production.

For more information, see the [Postings API documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api/).

### [](#asyncoperation "Copy link to heading")AsyncOperation

#### [](#_common_async_operations_BatchGetAsyncOperationsResponse_BatchGetAsyncOperations "Copy link to heading")BatchGet

**Deprecated** as of release **5.4**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0** *This method will serve no purpose once POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches:asyncCreate is removed.*

Retrieves multiple AsyncOperations. The IDs provided must belong to AsyncOperations returned by /v1/posting-instruction-batches:asyncCreate.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.posting\_instruction\_batches:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/posting-instruction-batches/async-operations:batchGet

##### [](#request_145 "Copy link to heading")Request

Body parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**request\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A unique ID generated by the client (payment processor) that is used for idempotency. The client must ensure a unique `request_id` is passed within their namespace (determined by `client_id`). Multiple requests with the same <`client_id` - `request_id`\> will receive the same response. Required.

 |
| 

**posting\_instruction\_batch**  
  
object

 | 

A posting instruction batch object. Required.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_id**  
  
string

 | 

Client Transactions must be unique for a given client ID. Required.  
\- Asynchronous API: Uniquely identifies a client of the Postings API. This must refer to an existing Postings API Client resource, which then determines the Kafka topic to which responses are published.  
\- Synchronous API: See the [Postings documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api#sync-using_the_api) for information about chaining Posting Instruction Batch requests.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_batch\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A correlation ID across different posting instruction batches. This drives no direct behaviour in Vault, but may be used as a filter for listing posting instruction batches. It is also used as the Kafka partition key for responses and events. The suggested use is to set the same `client_batch_id` across batches that contain posting instructions for the same financial transaction. Required.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.

\-For primary (initiating) posting instructions this must be unique for a given `client_id`  
\-For secondary (subsequent, chained) posting instructions this must refer to a previous `client_transaction_id`

**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

### [](#postinginstructionbatch "Copy link to heading")PostingInstructionBatch

#### [](#available_methods_58 "Copy link to heading")Available methods

-   [List](#_core_api_v1_posting_instruction_batches_ListPostingInstructionBatchesResponse_ListPostingInstructionBatches) Lists and filters posting instruction batches.
    
-   [Create](#_posting_api_v1_CreatePostingInstructionBatchResponse_CreatePostingInstructionBatch) Creates and returns a PostingInstructionBatch after submitting a CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest to the Postings API.
    
-   [Get](#_posting_api_v1_PostingInstructionBatch_GetPostingInstructionBatch) Retrieves a posting instruction batch by ID.
    
-   [Create (async)](#_common_async_operations_AsyncOperation_CreatePostingInstructionBatchAsync) Creates and returns an AsyncOperation to submit a PostingInstructionBatchRequest to the Postings API. **(Deprecated)**
    
-   [BatchGet](#_core_api_v1_posting_instruction_batches_BatchGetPostingInstructionBatchesResponse_BatchGetPostingInstructionBatches) Retrieves one or more posting instruction batches by ID.
    

#### [](#_core_api_v1_posting_instruction_batches_ListPostingInstructionBatchesResponse_ListPostingInstructionBatches "Copy link to heading")List

Lists and filters posting instruction batches. Performance of this endpoint is optimal by filtering customer `account_ids` and timerange on `value_timestamp`. Increasing the number of values or the number of request parameters will increase the response time. We recommend querying only customer accounts and not internal accounts through this endpoint, as internal accounts typically have a very large number of postings.

info

The following characteristics apply to the List endpoint:

-   When using this endpoint, there will be a short interval between a posting instruction batch being created, and it being visible in this endpoint
    
-   We write data into the read optimised schema before publishing [posting instruction batch events](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postinginstructionbatchcreatedevent). Posting instruction batches in this endpoints will be visible after those events are published.
    
-   If using Warm Storage [read replicas](/vault-core/5-8/EN/environment_and_installation/infrastructure_docs/vault_cloud_infrastructure/using_a_relational_database#multiple_database_setups) for lower latencies on this endpoint, there will be an additional interval between the event being published and the data being visible on this endpoint.
    
-   If there are multiple posting instructions in a batch with different value timestamps, only the *earliest* value timestamp will be considered in the filter
    
-   While we guarantee atomicity in Posting Instruction Batches, we do not guarantee the order in which the Posting Instructions will be arranged in the response.
    

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.posting\_instruction\_batches:read

**Pagination consistency guarantees:** Snapshot

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/posting-instruction-batches

**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
An OutboundAuthorisation, InboundAuthorisation, Transfer, OutboundHardSettlement or InboundHardSettlement specifies a `client_transaction_id` which already exists in the namespace of the `client_id`.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_DOES\_NOT\_EXIST:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment, Settlement, Release is referring to a non existent client transaction.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_ADJUSTMENT\_YIELDS\_AUTHORISATION\_WITH\_NEGATIVE\_AMOUNT:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment yields an authorisation with a negative amount.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_CLOSED:**  
An instruction is attempting to mutate a client transaction that has been closed.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_INVALID\_OPERATION:**  
An instruction is being added to a client transaction where the `value_timestamp` is not strictly later than the current latest instruction, or the instruction being processed would create a client transaction which has a combination of CustomInstructions and other instruction types.

**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_ACCOUNT\_STATUS\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s target account is in a status that doesn’t allow postings (for example: CLOSED, or PENDING).  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_UNSUPPORTED\_DENOMINATION:**  
The instruction’s target account does not support the posted denomination.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_PAYMENT\_DEVICE\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s payment device token resolved to a payment device that has an invalid status as of this batch’s value\_timestamp.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_MULTIPLE\_PROCESSING\_GROUPS:**  
The instruction affects multiple accounts that do not all share the same processing group.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_INTERNAL\_ACCOUNT\_PROCESSING\_LABEL\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s internal account processing label is not present.

The type of restriction violation. For instructions instructed prior to Vault version 5.4, this will be returned as `RESTRICTION_VIOLATION_TYPE_UNKNOWN`.  
  
**Enum values**  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_UNKNOWN:**  
An unknown restriction type.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_PREVENT\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which prevents credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_PREVENT\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which prevents debits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_REVIEW\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which requires reviewing credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_REVIEW\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which requires reviewing debits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_LIMIT\_CREDITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which limits credits.  
**RESTRICTION\_VIOLATION\_TYPE\_LIMIT\_DEBITS:**  
A restriction violation type that was caused by a restriction which limits debits.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for backdated and future-dated instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this PostingInstruction will be booked. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the `insertion_timestamp`. Should only be set for back-booked and future-booked instructions and must be between 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and the current time + 90 calendar days, inclusive. Defaults to the `insertion_timestamp` in UTC.

custom\_instruction.  
postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |

posting\_instruction\_batches\[\].  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the processing of the posting instruction batch.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_ACCEPTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been accepted and Postings have been committed to the ledger.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been rejected and no Postings have been committed to the ledger.

CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest contains invalid arguments and the request cannot be processed. See the error message for more details. Cannot Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INTERNAL:**  
An internal error occurred due to unexpected condition while processing the request. Can Retry.

A time to live expiry error occured because the requested `time_to_live` timestamp has expired. Cannot Retry.

#### [](#_posting_api_v1_CreatePostingInstructionBatchResponse_CreatePostingInstructionBatch "Copy link to heading")Create

Creates and returns a PostingInstructionBatch after submitting a CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest to the Postings API. Useful for high priority Postings.

chat\_bubble

There is also a Kafka-based asynchronous API, used for low-priority Postings. For more information, see the [Postings API documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api).

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.posting\_instruction\_batches:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches

##### [](#request_147 "Copy link to heading")Request

Body parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**request\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A unique ID generated by the client (payment processor) that is used for idempotency. The client must ensure a unique `request_id` is passed within their namespace (determined by `client_id`). Multiple requests with the same <`client_id` - `request_id`\> will receive the same response. Required.

 |
| 

**dry\_run**  
  
boolean

 | 

If true, the request will be executed with no side effects:  
\-Synchronous API: A PostingInstructionBatch will be returned  
\-Asynchronous API: A PostingInstructionBatch will be published to the response topic as defined by the Postings API Client ID  
In either case, no PostingInstructionBatch will be created and no PostingInstructionBatchCreatedEvent will be published to the event topic.

 |
| 

**posting\_instruction\_batch**  
  
object

 | 

A posting instruction batch object. Required.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_id**  
  
string

 | 

Client Transactions must be unique for a given client ID. Required.  
\- Asynchronous API: Uniquely identifies a client of the Postings API. This must refer to an existing Postings API Client resource, which then determines the Kafka topic to which responses are published.  
\- Synchronous API: See the [Postings documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api#sync-using_the_api) for information about chaining Posting Instruction Batch requests.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**client\_batch\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A correlation ID across different posting instruction batches. This drives no direct behaviour in Vault, but may be used as a filter for listing posting instruction batches. It is also used as the Kafka partition key for responses and events. The suggested use is to set the same `client_batch_id` across batches that contain posting instructions for the same financial transaction. Required.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**posting\_instructions\[\]**  
  
array \[object\]

 | 

A non-empty list of posting instruction objects to be processed atomically. Required.

 |

string

 | 

Set by the client. This is the ID of the client transaction this posting instruction is creating or mutating. Required.  
  
\-For primary (initiating) posting instructions this must be unique for a given `client_id`  
\-For secondary (subsequent, chained) posting instructions this must refer to a previous `client_transaction_id`

 |

A delta amount. The sign of the delta can be given explicitly (`"+3.40"`, `"-20"`) or implicitly if it is positive (e.g "3.40" is the same as "+3.40").  
  
*The amount of the AuthorisationAdjustment, which can be specified as a delta (the difference between the previous amount and the new amount) or as a new total authorised amount. On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.

**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_UNKNOWN:**  
The posting phase is not set which will result in a validation error.  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_PENDING\_INCOMING:**  
The posting is pending incoming (soft posting).  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_PENDING\_OUTGOING:**

**POSTING\_PHASE\_COMMITTED:**

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
custom\_instruction.  
postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**batch\_details**  
  
map \[string: string\]

 | 

Stores metadata related to the posting instruction batch resource. These details can also be retrieved in the posting instruction resource. Optional.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

**time\_to\_live**  
  
dateTime

 | 

\-Synchronous API: Not supported.  
\-Asynchronous API: Specifies a time after which the request generates an error with a POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_TTL\_EXPIRED error type. Optional.

string

 | 

A key used as a best-effort lock to prevent CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest with the same shard\_key from racing each other. For example, this can be used for multiple CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequests targeting the same account or plan to prevent retries from occurring, reducing the overall request latency. For a posting instruction batch that targets a single customer account, use the `account_id` or `payment_device_token` id. For a posting instruction batch that targets an account which is supervised, use the `plan_id`.

 |

**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 | 

The type of violation.

**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
An OutboundAuthorisation, InboundAuthorisation, Transfer, OutboundHardSettlement or InboundHardSettlement specifies a `client_transaction_id` which already exists in the namespace of the `client_id`.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_DOES\_NOT\_EXIST:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment, Settlement, Release is referring to a non existent client transaction.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_ADJUSTMENT\_YIELDS\_AUTHORISATION\_WITH\_NEGATIVE\_AMOUNT:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment yields an authorisation with a negative amount.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_CLOSED:**  
An instruction is attempting to mutate a client transaction that has been closed.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_INVALID\_OPERATION:**  
An instruction is being added to a client transaction where the `value_timestamp` is not strictly later than the current latest instruction, or the instruction being processed would create a client transaction which has a combination of CustomInstructions and other instruction types.

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
posting\_instructions\[\].  
custom\_instruction.  
postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**batch\_details**  
  
map \[string: string\]

 | 

Stores metadata related to the posting instruction batch resource. These details can also be retrieved in the posting instruction resource. Optional.

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the processing of the posting instruction batch.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_ACCEPTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been accepted and Postings have been committed to the ledger.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been rejected and no Postings have been committed to the ledger.

| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
error.  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of error returned.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest contains invalid arguments and the request cannot be processed. See the error message for more details. Cannot Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INTERNAL:**  
An internal error occurred due to unexpected condition while processing the request. Can Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_TTL\_EXPIRED:**  
A time to live expiry error occured because the requested `time_to_live` timestamp has expired. Cannot Retry.

#### [](#_posting_api_v1_PostingInstructionBatch_GetPostingInstructionBatch "Copy link to heading")Get

Retrieves a posting instruction batch by ID.

**Permission Scopes:** core:read, core.posting\_instruction\_batches:read

**Endpoint:** GET /v1/posting-instruction-batches/{id}

##### [](#request_148 "Copy link to heading")Request

Path parameters  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**id**  
  
string

 | 

The ID of the posting instruction batch to retrieve.

 |

##### [](#response_84 "Copy link to heading")Response

Response fields  
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
**id**  
  
string

 | 

Uniquely identifies a posting instruction batch in Vault.

 |
| 

**create\_request\_id**  
  
string

 | 

The `request_id` of the `create-posting-instruction-batch` request.

 |
| 

**client\_id**  
  
string

 | 

Client Transactions must be unique for a given client ID. Required.  
\- Asynchronous API: Uniquely identifies a client of the Postings API. This must refer to an existing Postings API Client resource, which then determines the Kafka topic to which responses are published.  
\- Synchronous API: See the [Postings documentation](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/postings_api#sync-using_the_api) for information about chaining Posting Instruction Batch requests.

 |
| 

**client\_batch\_id**  
  
string

 | 

A correlation ID across different posting instruction batches. This drives no direct behaviour in Vault, but may be used as a filter for listing posting instruction batches. It is also used as the Kafka partition key for responses and events. The suggested use is to set the same `client_batch_id` across batches that contain posting instructions for the same financial transaction. Required.

 |
| 

**posting\_instructions\[\]**  
  
array \[object\]

 | 

A non-empty list of posting instruction objects to be processed atomically. Required.

 |

string

 | 

Set by the client. This is the ID of the client transaction this posting instruction is creating or mutating. Required.  
  
\-For primary (initiating) posting instructions this must be unique for a given `client_id`  
\-For secondary (subsequent, chained) posting instructions this must refer to a previous `client_transaction_id`

posting\_instructions\[\].  
committed\_postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

Captures rejection reasons caused by posting logic validity checks. For example: Cannot adjust an authorisation that has already been settled.

 |
| 

posting\_instructions\[\].  
posting\_violations\[\].  
**type**  
  
enum

 | 

The type of violation.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_ALREADY\_EXISTS:**  
An OutboundAuthorisation, InboundAuthorisation, Transfer, OutboundHardSettlement or InboundHardSettlement specifies a `client_transaction_id` which already exists in the namespace of the `client_id`.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_DOES\_NOT\_EXIST:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment, Settlement, Release is referring to a non existent client transaction.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_ADJUSTMENT\_YIELDS\_AUTHORISATION\_WITH\_NEGATIVE\_AMOUNT:**  
An AuthorisationAdjustment yields an authorisation with a negative amount.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_CLOSED:**  
An instruction is attempting to mutate a client transaction that has been closed.  
**POSTING\_VIOLATION\_CLIENT\_TRANSACTION\_INVALID\_OPERATION:**  
An instruction is being added to a client transaction where the `value_timestamp` is not strictly later than the current latest instruction, or the instruction being processed would create a client transaction which has a combination of CustomInstructions and other instruction types.

The instruction’s target account is in a status that doesn’t allow postings (for example: CLOSED, or PENDING).  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_UNSUPPORTED\_DENOMINATION:**  
The instruction’s target account does not support the posted denomination.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_PAYMENT\_DEVICE\_INVALID:**  
The instruction’s payment device token resolved to a payment device that has an invalid status as of this batch’s value\_timestamp.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_MULTIPLE\_PROCESSING\_GROUPS:**  
The instruction affects multiple accounts that do not all share the same processing group.  
**ACCOUNT\_VIOLATION\_INTERNAL\_ACCOUNT\_PROCESSING\_LABEL\_NOT\_PRESENT:**  
The instruction’s internal account processing label is not present.

 | 

A delta amount. The sign of the delta can be given explicitly (`"+3.40"`, `"-20"`) or implicitly if it is positive (e.g "3.40" is the same as "+3.40").  
  
*The amount of the AuthorisationAdjustment, which can be specified as a delta (the difference between the previous amount and the new amount) or as a new total authorised amount. On a response, it is recommended to inspect the `delta_amount` and `authorised_amount` fields as they contain the same information but, unlike the `adjustment_amount.amount` or `adjustment_amount.replacement_amount` fields, they are guaranteed to be set on an accepted PostingInstructionBatch.

string

**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_UNKNOWN:**  
The posting phase is not set which will result in a validation error.  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_PENDING\_INCOMING:**  
The posting is pending incoming (soft posting).  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_PENDING\_OUTGOING:**  
The posting is pending outgoing (soft posting).  
**POSTING\_PHASE\_COMMITTED:**  
The posting is committed (hard posting).

posting\_instructions\[\].  
custom\_instruction.  
postings\[\].  
**internal\_account\_processing\_label**  
  
string

 | 

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. You also cannot instruct a CustomInstruction in which labels are used in all its postings.  
  
**Multiple Processing Groups are only available as an Extension.**

 |
| 

**batch\_details**  
  
map \[string: string\]

 | 

Stores metadata related to the posting instruction batch resource. These details can also be retrieved in the posting instruction resource. Optional.

 |
| 

**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

**status**  
  
enum

 | 

The status of the processing of the posting instruction batch.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN:**  
Default value.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_ACCEPTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been accepted and Postings have been committed to the ledger.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_STATUS\_REJECTED:**  
The PostingInstructionBatch has been rejected and no Postings have been committed to the ledger.

enum

The type of error returned.  
  
**Enum values**  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INVALID\_ARGUMENT:**  
CreatePostingInstructionBatchRequest contains invalid arguments and the request cannot be processed. See the error message for more details. Cannot Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_INTERNAL:**  
An internal error occurred due to unexpected condition while processing the request. Can Retry.  
**POSTING\_INSTRUCTION\_BATCH\_ERROR\_TYPE\_TTL\_EXPIRED:**  
A time to live expiry error occured because the requested `time_to_live` timestamp has expired. Cannot Retry.

#### [](#_common_async_operations_AsyncOperation_CreatePostingInstructionBatchAsync "Copy link to heading")Create (async)

**Deprecated** as of release **5.4**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0** *Use POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches instead.*

Creates and returns an AsyncOperation to submit a PostingInstructionBatchRequest to the Postings API. The Postings API is idempotent to duplicate PostingInstructionBatchRequest, and will respond idempotently to PostingInstructionBatchRequest messages with the same <client\_id-request\_id>. The CreatePostingInstructionBatchAsync endpoint is not idempotent and will create multiple AsyncOperation resources on duplicate calls.

warning

-   Create (async) should only be used for testing purposes - it is not supported in a production environment.
    
-   As of Vault Core 5.0 onwards, this does not send any outcome to the `response_topic`. The status of the posting instruction batch request can be checked by calling BatchGetAsyncOperations on the AsyncOperation ID.
    

**Permission Scopes:** core:write, core.posting\_instruction\_batches:write

**Endpoint:** POST /v1/posting-instruction-batches:asyncCreate

You can use a processing label to specify an Internal Account as part of a Custom Instruction instead of directly referencing an account ID. If you use a processing label in a CustomInstruction, there must be at least one posting in the same instruction that does not use a label, using the account\_id instead. The internal account then resolves using the processing group of the account identified by this account\_id. If a posting of a CustomInstruction using a processing label does not contain an account\_id, this request will fail. posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**value\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Specifies the time at which all committed postings of this batch’s posting instructions will affect balances. For most cases, including real time payments or fund movements, this does not require setting and will default to the generated `insertion_timestamp`. Only backdating of posting instruction batches is supported; this means that you cannot set them to be in the future, as determined by the clock of the ledger service. The earliest allowed value is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Optional; defaults to the insertion timestamp in UTC.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the value\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*

 |
| 

posting\_instruction\_batch.  
**booking\_timestamp**  
  
dateTime

 | 

Optional. Specifies the booking time of all committed postings of this batch’s Posting Instructions. Defaults to `value_timestamp` (which, in turn, defaults to `insertion_timestamp`). Can only be used for back-booked Posting Instruction Batches (PIBs), and can only be set if `value_timestamp` is also passed in the request; in which case `booking_timestamp` must be later than `value_timestamp`.  
  
**Deprecated** as of release **5.5**, and will be removed no earlier than release **7.0**  
*This field is replaced by the booking\_timestamp in the PostingInstruction. Deprecated only in the Postings API - not deprecated in the Postings Migration API.*
