## [](#core_streaming_api "Copy link to heading")Core Streaming API

### [](#overview "Copy link to heading")Overview

Vault Core natively supports real-time event sourcing from its core services. As the state of Vault Core is comprised of the states of a series of core resources (such as accounts, balances, products, and customers), the Vault Core Streaming API broadcasts events relating to mutations of each resource throughout its lifecycle.

These events are emitted as Kafka messages to a series of client-facing Kafka topics. Downstream services subscribing to such topics can be:

-   Data pipelines that perform Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) operations for financial reporting
    
-   Machine Learning services that perform fraud checks
    
-   Services that push customer notifications
    
-   Data warehousing modules
    

The Vault Core Streaming API lets you track the lifecycle of Vault Core resources by listening to a series of Kafka events that reflect all mutations of Vault Core’s state. These events are typically (but not limited to):

-   Resource creation (for example `create account`)
    
-   Resource mutation (for example `change contract parameter`)
    

#### [](#message_payload "Copy link to heading")Message payload

Each type of mutation is a separate Kafka topic in the Vault Core Streaming API. The message payload contains:

-   The ID of the resource involved
    
-   The resource field that has been altered; or
    
-   The whole resource object if a resource has been created (the schema of the resource is the same as the schema in the Vault Core API)
    

The update message that is sent when a resource is altered will contain either only those fields which have been mutated, or the complete state of the full resource. This will vary depending on the resource involved.

chat\_bubble

If you want to query the full resource, you can use the `Journal Events` API to replay the series of resource update events. There are some limitations to be aware of:

-   A Kafka retention period is set on all Kafka topics created by Vault Core; this is seven days by default, while some topics are set to a shorter period
    
-   Any Kafka messages that are older than this retention period will not be available
    
-   You can only use the Journal Events API to replay events that have occurred in the last seven days, and replayed Journal Events only contain the partial resource
    
-   If events occurred more than seven days ago, then you need to apply the more recent events to a persisted state of the resource as it was before the seven-day window
    

#### [](#message_formats "Copy link to heading")Message formats

The supported message formats are JSON or Google Protobuf. The required format is set when your Vault Core instance is configured.

#### [](#downloading_the_proto_files "Copy link to heading")Downloading the proto files

info

If you are using the Protobuf message format, download the schemas you need to integrate with the Core Streaming API.

Download download

chat\_bubble

Thought Machine guarantees API backwards compatibility at the proto level but not for code generated from those protos. Due to the varying output of available proto compilers, any code that is autogenerated from our proto files is not guaranteed to be backwards compatible with code that was autogenerated from proto files delivered with a previous version of Vault Core (including minor versions).

### [](#event_reconciliation "Copy link to heading")Event reconciliation

Event reconciliation provides a mechanism for consumers of the Vault Core Streaming APIs to verify that all events published to certain topics have been received (as opposed to reconciling any side effects resulting from the processing of such events).

This reconciliation is particularly useful following a timeout or processing failures where there is no way of easily identifying which events may have been missed; for example, during a data migration into Vault Core.

This section covers the following aspects of event reconciliation:

-   The [mechanisms](#mechanisms_for_event_reconciliation) that are available for event reconciliation
    
-   The [topics](#topics_that_can_be_reconciled) that can be reconciled using event reconciliation
    
-   The [checksum algorithm](#checksum_algorithm) used for event reconciliation
    
-   The [errors](#event_reconciliation_errors) that can occur during event reconciliation
    

#### [](#mechanisms_for_event_reconciliation "Copy link to heading")Mechanisms for event reconciliation

There are three mechanisms available for reconciling events:

-   Detection of missed events (using the `change_id` or `sequence_number`)
    
-   Detection of missed events (using Windowing)
    
-   Event replay
    

##### [](#detection_of_missed_events_using_change_id_or_sequence_number "Copy link to heading")Detection of missed events (using change ID or sequence number)

The publication to the streaming API of a monotonically and continuously increasing sequence number, which may be either the `change_id` for a resource or the `sequence_number` for a related resource, allows the detection of missed events in the stream as these are processed. Any gap in the sequence of change (or related resource) IDs would highlight that one or more events have been missed.

chat\_bubble

Detection over the whole stream is not possible using the `change_id` (or `sequence_number`) only. In particular: - If the creation event for a resource has been missed, there is no immediate way of detecting this from the `change_id` or `sequence_number`. It would only become apparent when there is a subsequent update event for the resource and no creation event has yet been processed. - There is no immediate way to detect that the most recent update event for a resource has been missed. It would only become apparent when there is a subsequent update for the resource, at which point the gap in sequence numbers can be detected.

These limitations can be overcome using Windowing.

##### [](#detection_of_missed_events_using_windowing "Copy link to heading")Detection of missed events (using Windowing)

To fully reconcile an external system against Vault Core, use Windowing.

Calling [GET /v1/journal-events:checksum](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#journaleventschecksum) enables clients to request a summary of the state changes of all Vault Core resources of a type within a specific historic time period. A call to this endpoint will return both the number of state changes committed to Vault Core within the specified time period (window) and a checksum that uniquely identifies the set of events generated as a consequence to those changes (see [Checksum Algorithm](#checksum_algorithm) for more details of the algorithm used in the checksum).

The time reference used in this context is always the time when the state change is committed into Vault Core which is exposed to clients in the streaming API events (`timestamp`).

##### [](#event_replay "Copy link to heading")Event replay

If missed events were detected using either the `change_id` or the `sequence_number`, these events can be replayed by calling [POST /v1/journal-events:replay](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#JournalEvent). Calling this endpoint will cause the system to replay an exact copy of the original events for downstream consumption, with an added batch ID header with key `X-JournalEventsBatch-ID`.

chat\_bubble

Events can be replayed for the `resource_type`s listed within the [JournalEvent endpoint](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#journalevent).

To replay any `resource_type`s, use one of the following identifiers:

-   `event_id`
    
-   `resource_id` AND `change_id`
    
-   `related_resource_id` AND `sequence_number`
    

If missed events were detected using windowing, call [GET /v1/journal-events](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#journalevent) to retrieve a paginated list of all journal events contained within the time window. By comparing the result of this call with your record, you can identify which events are missed.

Replay these events by calling [POST /v1/journal-events:replay](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#JournalEvent) as described above when detecting missed events using either the `change_id` or the `sequence_number`. Duplicate identifiers in the `journal_events_to_replay` collection in the `ReplayJournalEventsRequest` are ignored and the corresponding events will only be replayed once.

#### [](#topics_that_can_be_reconciled "Copy link to heading")Topics that can be reconciled

The following Core Streaming API topics can be reconciled:

-   `vault.api.v1.postings.posting_instruction_batch.created`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v2.accounts.account.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_update.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_update_batch.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.balances.account_balance.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v2.balances.balance.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.contracts.contract_notification.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.flags.flag.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.parameters.parameter.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.parameters.parameter_value.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.postings.enriched_posting_instruction_batch.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.restrictions.restriction_set.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.scheduler.operation.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.vault_jobs.job.events`
    

The reconciliation mechanism that can be used depends on how events are published to the topics. There are three categories:

-   [Mutable resource topics](#mutable_resource_topics); published when the state of a Vault Core resource mutates
    
-   [Immutable resource topics](#immutable_resource_topics); published when corresponding Vault Core resources are created
    
-   [Mutable related resource topics](#mutable_related_resource_topics); published when the corresponding Vault Core resources change in relation to an associated resource
    

##### [](#mutable_resource_topics "Copy link to heading")Mutable resource topics

Every Vault Core resource is identified by a unique `resource_id`. An event is published to a topic when the state of a Vault Core resource mutates. For example, Flag events are published to the `vault.core_api.v1.flags.flag.events` topic when a Flag resource is created or updated). Each creation or mutation event is associated in the streaming API to a monotonically and continuously increasing integer called the `change_id`, which is specific to the mutated resource. The creation event for any Vault Core resource therefore has a `change_id` of `0`. The first time that resource is mutated, the corresponding event will have a change ID of `1`, and so on.

The following topics are mutable resource topics and can be reconciled using the `change_id` and the `resource_id`, or the `event_id`:

-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_update.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_update_batch.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v2.accounts.account.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.parameters.parameter_value.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.vault_jobs.job.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.restrictions.restriction_set.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.flags.flag.events`
    

##### [](#immutable_resource_topics "Copy link to heading")Immutable resource topics

Events are published to these topics when the corresponding Vault Core resources are created. (For example, enriched posting instruction batches events are published to the `vault.core_api.v1.postings.enriched_posting_instruction_batch.events` topic when an enriched posting instruction batch resource is created.) Detection of missed events for this sort of topic is not available as the change ID is set to `0` for all events.

The following topic is an immutable resource topic and can be reconciled using the event ID:

-   `vault.api.v1.postings.posting_instruction_batch.created`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.contracts.contract_notification.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.parameters.parameter.events`
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.postings.enriched_posting_instruction_batch.events`
    

##### [](#mutable_related_resource_topics "Copy link to heading")Mutable related resource topics

Events are published to these topics when the corresponding Vault Core resources change in respect to a related resource, called the `related_resource`. For example, account balance events are published to the `vault.core_api.v1.balances.account_balance.events` topic when the balance for a specific account resource is created or updated. Each creation or mutation event is associated in the streaming API to a monotonically and continuously increasing number called a `sequence_number`. The related Vault Core resource is identified by a `related_resource_id`.

The following topics are mutable related resource topics and can be reconciled using the `sequence_number` and the `related_resource_id`, or the `event_id`:

-   `vault.core_api.v1.scheduler.operation.events` (the related resource is the RESOURCE\_TYPE\_SCHEDULER\_TAG)
    
-   `vault.core_api.v1.balances.account_balance.events` (the related resource is the RESOURCE\_TYPE\_ACCOUNT)
    

chat\_bubble

RESOURCE\_TYPE\_SCHEDULER\_TAG and RESOURCE\_TYPE\_ACCOUNT are the only two resource types that can be used as related resources.

#### [](#event_reconciliation_errors "Copy link to heading")Event reconciliation errors

There are two errors that can occur when reconciling events:

-   InvalidArgument
    
-   NotFound
    

chat\_bubble

The errors described below describe `now()` as the time at which the Vault Core Journal Events API starts processing a request made to either the `GetJournalEventsChecksum` endpoint or to the `ListJournalEvents` endpoint.

##### [](#invalidargument "Copy link to heading")InvalidArgument

This error can be generated when any of the following conditions occur in the specified scenario:

-   The lower bound timestamp in the time window is earlier than seven days in the past (that is, `now()` - seven days) (`GetJournalEventsChecksum` and `ListJournalEvents`)
    
-   The upper bound timestamp in the time window is in the future (that is, greater or equal to `now()`) (`GetJournalEventsChecksum` and `ListJournalEvents`)
    
-   The `page_size` is not within 1 and 100, boundaries included (`ListJournalEvents`)
    
-   The `journal_events_to_replay` contains no identifiers (`ReplayJournalEvents`)
    
-   The `journal_events_to_replay` contains more than 100 identifiers (`ReplayJournalEvents`)
    
-   The `journal_events_to_replay` contains one or more IDs that cannot be used to reconcile the relevant topic (it contains a `change_id` and a `resource_id` but the topic can only be reconciled using a sequence number and a `related_resource_id`) (`ReplayJournalEvents`)
    
-   The time window contains more than 500k events when calculating the checksum (`GetJournalEventsChecksum`)
    

##### [](#notfound "Copy link to heading")NotFound

This error can be generated when the `journal_events_to_replay` contains one or more ids that are not in the Vault Core journal (`ReplayJournalEvents`)

#### [](#checksum_algorithm "Copy link to heading")Checksum algorithm

The events reconciliation checksum algorithm enables external verification that events consumed by downstream consumers of Vault Core (during a particular time window) match the internal state of Vault Core. The algorithm used to calculate the checksum in the [GetJournalEventsChecksum](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#journaleventschecksum) endpoint is described in this section.

The algorithm uses a hashing function and an XOR operation which makes its application commutative. Combining hashes using an XOR requires all `event_id`s to be the same length, so a preparatory processing step is required to ensure that all inputs to the XOR function for each `event_id` are the same length. The sha256 algorithm is used for this purpose.

The checksum is calculated using the following steps:

1.  Vault Core hashes each `event_id` using SHA256.
    
2.  Vault Core sequentially applies an XOR function on each hash from the previous result.
    
3.  Vault Core returns a hash of the final result as a hexadecimal string.
    

For example, for `event_id`s A, B, C, the result will be sha(XOR(XOR(sha(A), sha(B)), sha(C))).

lightbulb

The checksum algorithm within Vault Core will not operate with duplicated `event_id` values. For the algorithm to work correctly, remove any duplicate `event_id` values.

chat\_bubble

When calculating the Journal Events checksum for a specified period of time, Vault Core returns a checksum based on all events during that period regardless of the `journal_events[].published` status. This is because the checksum calculation considers all unpublished Journal Events retrieved during that window of time to be eventually published.

If you are using [Journal Events](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#journal_events) to detect and replay missed events over that period, you should therefore only replay ones that have `journal_events[].published` set to `true`.

#### [](#accountpostpostingexecutionfailureevent "Copy link to heading")AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent

`AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent`s are created if an Account’s `post_posting_code` Smart Contract hook execution fails. If this happens, a [`PostPostingFailure`](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) resource is created, and an `AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent` is produced to this topic.

Upon receiving an event on this topic, the Core API `ListPostPostingFailures` endpoint will return `PostPostingFailure` resources that were created due to this failed `post_posting_code` execution. If the Core API endpoint returns no resources, it is likely that the `RepublishPostPostingFailure` or `DeletePostPostingFailure` Core API endpoints have already been called. These endpoints will either retry or skip the `post_posting_code` execution, and remove the `PostPostingFailure` resource.

In rare cases, if a `post_posting_code` execution fails, and the creation of a [`PostPostingFailure`](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) resource in Vault Core also fails, then the List `PostPostingFailure` endpoint will return no [PostPostingFailure](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure)s, but an `AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent` may still be published to this topic.

### [](#account_events_version_2_topic "Copy link to heading")Account events version 2 topic

chat\_bubble

This section lists the Account events generated on the version 2 topic.

#### [](#accountevent_2 "Copy link to heading")AccountEvent

An `AccountEvent` is published to indicate the creation or mutation of an Account. We support:

-   Internal or Customer Account creation (AccountCreatedEvent)
    
-   Account updates (AccountUpdatedEvent)
    

chat\_bubble

In the event that a problem occurs when opening, converting or closing an Account, the Account will be updated, and the associated AccountUpdatedEvent will contain the error that caused the problem.

*Delivery*: At least once delivery guarantees.

#### [](#balanceevent "Copy link to heading")BalanceEvent

A `BalanceEvent` is created whenever a Customer Account’s live value balance or live booking balance changes. For a given PostingInstructionBatch with N PostingInstructions:

-   One event is generated for each unique booking or value timestamp per Customer Account
    
-   If multiple PostingInstructions within the same PostingInstructionBatch share the same value and booking timestamps for the same Customer Account, they will be merged into a single event
    

*Topic*: `vault.core_api.v2.balances.balance.events`

*Delivery*: At least once delivery guarantees.

chat\_bubble

To switch from the `AccountBalanceEvent` to the `BalanceEvent` stream, see the documentation [here](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/balances#switching_from_the_accountbalanceevent_to_the_balanceevent).

 |

int64

 |

 |
|

 | 

`google.protobuf.Timestamp`

 | 

The time the event was created.

 |
|

string

 |

 |

Default value.

**BALANCE\_UPDATE\_TYPE\_VALUE:**

Live value balance updated for the customer account.

**BALANCE\_UPDATE\_TYPE\_BOOKING:**

Live booking balance updated for the customer account.

 |
|

`core_api.v2.balances.Balance`

`posting_api.v1.PostingInstruction`

 |
| 

`booking_posting_instructions`

 | 

`posting_api.v1.PostingInstruction`

 | 

The Posting Instructions that have triggered this event by affecting the live booking balance for the account. If only subset of the Posting Instructions in a Posting Instruction Batch affect the live booking balance then only these instructions are present in this field.

 |
| 

`vault_version`

`versioning.SemVer`

int64

 | 

Sequence number will increment for any new *value* balance update event per account. This can be used when [switching](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/balances#switching_from_the_accountbalanceevent_to_the_balanceevent) from the `AccountBalanceEvent` stream to the `BalanceEvent` stream - the field will be equal to the corresponding `AccountBalanceEvent.related_resource.sequence_number`. The field will be 0 when only the booking balance is changing.

### [](#ledgerbalance_events "Copy link to heading")LedgerBalance events

#### [](#ledgerbalancebucketreassignmentevent "Copy link to heading")LedgerBalanceBucketReassignmentEvent

A `LedgerBalanceBucketReassignmentEvent` indicates that a Posting Instruction Batch has been assigned a Ledger Balance bucket that is different from its `insertion_timestamp` in the Postings Ledger. Affected Ledger Balances with a timestamp between the `ledger_insertion_timestamp` and `bucket_timestamp` will not include this Posting Instruction Batch.

*Topic*: `vault.core_api.v1.ledger_balances.bucket_reassignment.events`

*Delivery*: At least once delivery

  
| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 
`posting_instruction_batch_id`

 | 

string

 | 

The ID of the Posting Instruction Batch that has been reassigned to a new Ledger Balance bucket.

 |
| 

`ledger_insertion_timestamp`

 | 

`google.protobuf.Timestamp`

 | 

The time that the Posting Instruction Batch was inserted into the Postings Ledger in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |
| 

`bucket_timestamp`

 | 

`google.protobuf.Timestamp`

 | 

The Ledger Balance bucket that this Posting Instruction Batch has been assigned to. Each bucket timestamp represents the upper bound of a window of duration one second that is used to group Posting Instruction Batches together, in UTC. Formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

 |

`EnrichedPostingInstructionBatchEvent` wraps a PostingInstructionBatch with additional End of Day metadata. In order to produce this stream, you must first create a Calendar resource and specify it as the input calendar for the `EnrichedPostingInstructionBatchEvent` Kafka stream.

### [](#vault_jobs_events "Copy link to heading")Vault Jobs events

Vault Core generates the following events when it publishes their corresponding events to the Vault Core Streaming API:

-   `JobEvent` - on publishing a Vault Jobs event
    
-   `GroupEvent` - on publishing a Vault Jobs Groups event

###### [](#vault_jobstatus "Copy link to heading")Vault JobStatus

chat\_bubble

A Vault Job may not go through each `status` and supported statuses may vary based on the `service`. When listening for a specific status to trigger any downstream event you should consume both the `JobCreatedEvent` and `JobUpdatedEvent` as it is not guaranteed which event will contain the target `status`. For example, a `JobCreatedEvent` may have status `JOB_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS` or it may have status `JOB_STATUS_PENDING` and then a subsequent `JobUpdatedEvent` may change the status to `JOB_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS`.

 
| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
JOB\_STATUS\_UNKNOWN

 | 

The status of the Job is unknown.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_PENDING

 | 

The Job has not yet started.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_IN\_PROGRESS

 | 

The Job is in progress.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_SUCCEEDED

 | 

The Job has completed successfully.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_ABANDONED

 | 

All operations expected to execute for the Job were abandoned, because they were not required.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_ERRORED

 | 

The Job has completed with one or more errors.

 |
| 

JOB\_STATUS\_EXPIRED

 | 

The Job has expired.

 |

#### [](#fieldmask "Copy link to heading")FieldMask

`FieldMask` represents a set of symbolic field paths in string array. For example:

 
| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 
`f`

 | 

Represents a field in a root message.

 |
| 

`a` and `b`

 | 

Represent fields in the message found in `f`.

 |
| 

`d`

 | 

Represents a field found in the message in `f.b`.

 |

Field masks are used to specify a subset of fields that should be, or have been, modified by an update operation. Field masks have the following JSON encoding:

  
| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 
paths

 | 

string array

 | 

The set of field mask paths.

 |

## [](#core_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Core DLQs

### [](#accounts_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Accounts DLQs

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_api_v1_accounts_account_post_posting_execution_failure_events_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core\_api.v1.accounts.account\_post\_posting\_execution\_failure.events.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#account_events)

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.post_posting.execution.account.failure.events`

##### [](#what_failed "Copy link to heading")What failed?

There was a problem executing an account’s [post\_posting\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/supervisor_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#post_posting_hook) (CLv4) / [post\_posting\_code](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_3xx/supervisor_contracts_api_reference3xx/hooks#post_posting_code) (CLv3), leading to a [PostPostingFailure](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) resource being created and a message being published to the internal `vault.core.post_posting.execution.account.failure.events` topic. Vault Core attempted to consume this message and publish an [AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#account_events) message to the public `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_post_posting_execution_failure.events.failures` topic but this failed so message is annotated with DLQ metadata and published to this topic.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

There will be a missing [AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#account_events) message on `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_post_posting_execution_failure.events` topic. There may be a missing [PostPostingFailure](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) resource meaning an account that should be blocked may not be blocked from further `post_posting_hook`/`post_posting_code` Smart Contract hook executions. Look at the headers of the message in the DLQ. Query the Core API [PostPostingFailure](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) endpoints to check if there are [PostPostingFailure](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#postpostingfailure) resources created.

##### [](#possible_failure_reasons_and_recoveries "Copy link to heading")Possible failure reasons and recoveries

For any error message seen on this DLQ, you must contact Thought Machine.

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_api_v1_accounts_account_schedule_job_execution_failure_events_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core\_api.v1.accounts.account\_schedule\_job\_execution\_failure.events.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_2 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[AccountScheduleJobExecutionFailureEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#account_events)

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from_2 "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.schedule.execution.account.failure.events`

##### [](#what_failed_2 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

There was a problem executing an account’s [scheduled\_event\_hook](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/supervisor_contracts_api_reference4xx/hooks#scheduled_event_hook) (CLv4)/[scheduled\_code](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_3xx/supervisor_contracts_api_reference3xx/hooks#scheduled_code) (CLv3), leading to an `AccountScheduleJobExecutionFailureEvent` message being put on an internal failures topic. Vault Core attempted to consume this message and publish the `AccountPostPostingExecutionFailureEvent` to the public `vault.core_api.v1.accounts.account_schedule_job_execution_failure.events` topic, but this failed. As a result, the message is annotated with DLQ metadata and published to this topic.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_2 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

We expect that this will never happen, because we control both the producer and the consumer side of this topic. If it does happen, it is due to a bug and you should contact Thought Machine.

##### [](#possible_failure_reasons_and_recoveries_2 "Copy link to heading")Possible failure reasons and recoveries

For any error message seen on this DLQ, you must contact Thought Machine.

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_contracts_journeys_account_schedule_responses_dlq "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core.contracts.journeys.account\_schedule.responses.dlq

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_3 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

This is an internal DLQ and the message type is internal.

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from_3 "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.contracts.journeys.account_schedule.responses`

##### [](#what_failed_3 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

A schedule outcome response could not be unmarshaled into the expected proto type.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_3 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

We expect that this will never happen, because we control both the producer and the consumer side of this topic. If it does happen, it is due to a bug - contact Thought Machine.

### [](#accounts_v2_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Accounts v2 DLQs

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_4 "Copy link to heading")What Message has been sent to the DLQ?

The unexpected (internal) message which could not be converted into a [v2 AccountEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#account_events_v2_topic).

##### [](#what_failed_4 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

Any event which could not be converted to a message on the vault.core\_api.v2.accounts.account.events topic.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_4 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

The Account service will continue to run, but there may be no corresponding Kafka event on the successful event topic (`vault.core_api.v2.accounts.account.events`).

##### [](#possible_failure_reasons_and_recoveries_3 "Copy link to heading")Possible failure reasons and recoveries

If the cause of the unexpected message cannot be identified, then please contact Thought Machine. Logs from the following Deployments' Pods at around the time of the DLQ message being published will be helpful:

-   Core-stream-api
    
-   accounts-journal-poller
    
-   accounts
    
-   accounts-retry-executor
    
-   accounts-v2-to-v1-events-processor

### [](#contract_events_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Contract Events DLQs

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_api_v1_contract_events_contract_execution_events_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core\_api.v1.contract\_events.contract\_execution.events.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_8 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[ContractExecutionEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#contract_execution_events)

##### [](#what_failed_8 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

There was an error executing a Smart or Supervisor Contract hook, leading to the creation of a ContractExecution resource with an error status. During the publishing of the ContractExecutionCreatedEvent to the corresponding event stream topic, a new error occurred.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_8 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

There is a missing ContractExecutionCreatedEvent for a ContractExecution that was created with an error status. The underlying ContractExecution resource was still created. However, any external integration that is listening to this event topic will not be notified with a new message for this ContractExecution. The creation of ContractExecutions is [best-effort](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/running_contracts_in_production#contract_events_api_data_consistency), so no external integration should be solely relying on the ContractExecutionCreatedEvent topic for notification of contract execution errors. The ContractExecution resource is used for observability only, not financial processing, therefore there should be no financial impact.

##### [](#possible_failure_reasons_and_recoveries_7 "Copy link to heading")Possible failure reasons and recoveries

Inspect the message headers and contents, which may contain an error message. It is likely there was an issue unmarshalling the ContractExecution contents into the expected protocol buffer type. It may be helpful to examine logs from the following deployments’ Pods at around the time of the DLQ message being published:

-   core-stream-api
    
-   contract-events-collector
    
-   contract-events-journal-poller
    

The ContractExecution resource is for observability only, not financial processing, therefore there should be no financial impact. However, any error message seen on this DLQ indicates a bug, so you must contact Thought Machine.

### [](#contract_notification_events_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Contract notification events DLQs

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_api_v1_contracts_contract_notification_events_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core\_api.v1.contracts.contract\_notification.events.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_9 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[ContractNotificationEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#contract_notification_events)

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from_7 "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.contracts.contract_notification.events`

##### [](#what_failed_9 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

A message is published to the DLQ if there was a problem publishing a Contract Notification event from a Smart or Supervisor contract executing a hook containing the [instruct\_notification](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_3xx/supervisor_contracts_api_reference3xx/vault#instruct_notification) directive (in Contracts Language API version 3) or [AccountNotificationDirective](/vault-core/5-8/EN/reference/contracts/contracts_api_4xx/common_types_4xx/classes#accountnotificationdirective) (in version 4).

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_9 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

There will be no corresponding Kafka event on the successful event topic `vault.core_api.v1.contracts.contract_notification.events`. This should not have an effect on the behaviour of Vault Core but should be taken into account when dealing with external components that are listening to this topic.

##### [](#possible_failure_reasons_and_recoveries_8 "Copy link to heading")Possible failure reasons and recoveries

For any error message seen on this DLQ, you must contact Thought Machine.

### [](#customer_events_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Customer events DLQs

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_api_v1_customers_customer_created_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.api.v1.customers.customer.created.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_10 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[CustomerCreatedEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#customer_events)

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from_8 "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.customer.events`

##### [](#what_failed_10 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

A message is published to the DLQ if there was a problem publishing a Customer event which reflects the creation of a Customer within Vault Core.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_10 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

The Customer will have been created within Vault Core, but there will be no corresponding Kafka event on the successful event topic (`vault.api.v1.customers.customer.created`). This should not have an effect on the behaviour of Vault Core but should be taken into account when dealing with external components that are listening to these topics.

For any error message seen on this DLQ, you must contact Thought Machine.

### [](#scheduler_events_dlqs "Copy link to heading")Scheduler events DLQs

#### [](#dlq_name_vault_core_api_v1_scheduler_operation_events_failures "Copy link to heading")DLQ name: vault.core\_api.v1.scheduler.operation.events.failures

##### [](#what_message_has_been_sent_to_the_dlq_13 "Copy link to heading")What message has been sent to the DLQ?

[OperationEvent](/vault-core/5-8/EN/api/core_api#scheduler_events)

##### [](#what_topic_was_the_message_originally_consumed_from_11 "Copy link to heading")What topic was the message originally consumed from?

`vault.core.scheduler.operation.events`

##### [](#what_failed_13 "Copy link to heading")What failed?

A message is published to the DLQ if there was a problem publishing a Scheduler Operation event that reflects the execution of a tagged set of schedules.

##### [](#what_is_the_impact_13 "Copy link to heading")What is the impact?

There will be no impact on the Scheduler, which will continue with the execution of the schedules, but there will be no corresponding Kafka event on the successful event topic (`vault.core_api.v1.scheduler.operation.events`). This should not have an effect on the behaviour of Vault Core but should be taken into account when dealing with external components that are listening to this topic.
